37693bd566ffb575: KUALA LUMPUR: Chinese actor Wang Yibo is making the most of his time in Malaysia, balancing food trips with preparations for an upcoming race.
The 29-year-old recently arrived in the country to get ready for the 2026 China GT Championship season finale, which takes place at the Sepang International Circuit from Nov 6 to 8.
While in the city, Wang was spotted enjoying the local food scene.
On Wednesday (Oct 14), he dined with his team at a bak kut teh restaurant in Pudu.
Later that evening, he carried on his culinary adventure at Jalan Alor, where he was seen eating durian.
When he is not trying local treats, Wang has been at the Sepang International Circuit to get familiar with the track.
The upcoming event marks his very first overseas competition as a professional racing driver.
Wang first stepped into motorsports at the Michelin GPGP Grand Prix in Beijing in 2019, before switching to GT car racing in 2024.
Before hitting the race track, Wang started his career in show business in 2014 as the main rapper and dancer for the South Korean-Chinese boy band Uniq.
He made his acting debut in the 2016 film MBA Partners and starred in popular dramas including The Untamed (2019), Legend Of Fei (2020), and Hidden Blade (2023).
9ba049ca078c29bc: TIANJIN, Oct 16 — Malaysia is ready to help Indonesia tackle widespread forest and land fires after President Prabowo Subianto agreed to accept offers of assistance from neighbouring countries.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Malaysia welcomed the Indonesian government’s openness to receiving foreign assistance to fight the fires.
He said that although Malaysia’s offer might be modest, Putrajaya remained committed to helping its neighbour in the spirit of friendship and strong bilateral ties.
“We are grateful to the Indonesian government and President Prabowo for being open to accepting foreign assistance to tackle the forest fires.
“Even though the help we have offered is small, Malaysia is prepared to send aid to assist our neighbour,” he said, adding that Malaysia valued Prabowo’s openness on the matter.
He made the remarks to Malaysian journalists during an afternoon tea session shortly before departing China today, following a five-day working visit.
Buildings are shrouded in haze from Indonesian fires in Kuala Lumpur on October 16, 2026. — AFP pic

Earlier, Indonesian Foreign Ministry official Arrmanatha Nasir reportedly said President Prabowo had approved offers of assistance from neighbouring countries, with technical discussions underway to determine how the aid would be delivered.
However, Arrmanatha did not specify which countries had offered assistance or what form it would take.
Malaysia had previously offered to deploy a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 personnel to help Indonesia tackle the fires.
On September 19, Ahmad Zahid said Prabowo had accepted the offer during a meeting the previous day in Hambalang, West Java. — Bernama
692c6eaeec511f50: PUTRAJAYA: The Road Transport Department (JPJ) will cooperate with the police to ensure a thorough and transparent investigation into a crash that killed one of its personnel and seriously injured another near the Senawang exit on the North-South Expressway last night.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said action would be taken against any party found to have violated the law or committed misconduct.

"If there are any legal violations, misconduct, or negligence identified through the investigation, action will be taken against the responsible parties in accordance with the provisions of the law and regulations in force," he said in a statement.
Loke extended his condolences to the family of Negri Sembilan RTD Enforcement Assistant Grade KP2 Mohd Azrul Rashid Yaakub, who was killed in the accident while on duty.
"Azrul's passing is a great loss, particularly to his family and colleagues. His sacrifice and dedication in carrying out his duties for the safety of road users will always be appreciated," he said.
He also wished Motor Vehicle Examiner Grade AB2 Nor Amirudin Rameli, who was seriously injured in the crash, a speedy recovery.
Loke said RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli had visited the families of both officers this morning to convey his condolences and offer support.
The Transport Ministry and RTD would continue to look into the welfare and needs of the deceased's family and the injured officer, including providing appropriate assistance, he added.
The crash occurred around 10.50pm when RTD personnel were inspecting a lorry parked on the emergency lane at KM256 of the southbound North-South Expressway near the Senawang exit.
A lorry driver approaching from behind veered out of control and crashed into the RTD sport utility vehicle (SUV) and the lorry being inspected.
acfe487665071fb4: JOHOR BARU: Firefighters are battling a blaze at an electrical substation in the Tebrau 4 Industrial Area in Jalan Kangkar Tebrau here, with several nearby areas experiencing power outages.
The Johor Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 6.10pm, with firefighters from the Tebrau Fire and Rescue station arriving at the scene six minutes later.
Eight firefighters and a fire engine were deployed to tackle the blaze.
No casualties had been reported as of the latest update, while firefighting operations were still underway.
Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), in a statement, said the fire at the Kangkar Tebrau main intake substation had disrupted electricity supply to several areas in Johor Jaya.
"Our technical team has been deployed to the site and is working to restore power to affected consumers," the statement read.

0b41b50427e9cb9a: ARAU, Oct 16 — The Perlis Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has recovered RM698,255.55 through forfeitures from 2024 to date.
Perlis MACC director Mohd Nor Adha Ab Gani said the state anti-graft agency opened 65 investigation papers (IPs), recorded 84 arrests and brought 37 charges to court during the period.

“According to the annual breakdown, 20 IPs were opened in 2024 involving 27 arrests and 13 charges, with a forfeiture value of RM323,872.55. In 2025, 22 investigation papers were opened, 34 arrests were recorded, and 16 charges were brought to court, with a forfeiture value of RM374,168.

“As for 2026, Perlis MACC opened 23 investigation papers, recorded 23 arrests, and brought eight charges to court, with a forfeiture value of RM215,” he was quoted as saying in a statement issued by Istana Arau today.
The statement said the outgoing director presented the figures to the Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail during a recent farewell ceremony at Istana Arau.
Mohd Nor Adha said Perlis MACC also focused on preventive measures, submitting 61 Governance Improvement Recommendations to federal and state departments and statutory bodies.
“These efforts aim to strengthen the public service delivery system, enhance organisational integrity, and close gaps and opportunities for corruption to occur,” he said.
He said Perlis MACC personnel had also received several accolades in recognition of their commitment and performance, including the Chief Commissioner Special Award for 2024 and 2025.
“Perlis MACC also won the Best KPI Management Award 2025 with an evaluation score of 97.45 per cent, besides securing third place for the Best Financial Management Award 2025.

“These achievements demonstrate the dedication of Perlis MACC in balancing enforcement action with continuous preventive measures to foster an administrative environment of integrity, transparency, and accountability,” he said.
At the farewell ceremony, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra thanked Mohd Nor Adha for his service and commitment in leading Perlis MACC for two years and seven months, from March 1, 2024, until tomorrow.
His Royal Highness also congratulated him on his promotion and appointment as Terengganu MACC director, effective October 18.

The Raja Muda expressed hope that the experience Mohd Nor Adha gained in Perlis would help him in his new role and in continuing efforts to strengthen integrity, governance and anti-corruption initiatives. — Bernama

f66ec3fe733f60ee: KUALA LUMPUR: Cape EMS Bhd has signed a memorandum of agreement (MoA) with Taiwan's FIC Global Inc unit Pro3C (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd to support the latter's expansion in Johor's artificial intelligence (AI) manufacturing supply chain.
The agreement, signed on Oct 16, positions Cape EMS as Pro3C's local strategic partner, providing manufacturing infrastructure, supply chain management, facilities and operational support.

The collaboration supports Cape's CEB 2.0 transformation, aimed at improving facility utilisation, generating recurring revenue and shifting its electronics manufacturing services (EMS) business towards higher-value manufacturing.
Pro3C's manufacturing facility at i-Park @ Senai Airport City, which was opened on Oct 15, represents a first-phase investment of about US$50 million.
The plant manufactures components for 800G, 1.6T and 3.2T high-speed optical transceivers used in AI infrastructure, high-performance computing and data centres.
Pro3C currently operates eight surface-mount technology production lines with about 530 employees.
It plans to increase capacity by 125 per cent to 18 lines by 2027, with potential expansion of its manufacturing floor space by up to four times.
FIC Global is targeting revenue of up to US$2 billion from its Johor operations in 2027, subject to customer demand.

Cape EMS group managing director and chief executive officer Christina Tee said the collaboration presented an opportunity to revitalise its EMS business and strengthen its position in advanced electronics manufacturing.

The MoA also provides for a potential subscription by Pro3C or its nominee for redeemable convertible preference shares in Cape EMS, subject to separate commercial terms and regulatory and shareholder approvals.
939542f794babd1f: KUALA LUMPUR: The government supports efforts to strengthen Islamic scholarship, research and intellectual discourse to contribute to national governance and the well-being of the ummah, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

In a post on X, Anwar said this after receiving a courtesy call today from a delegation from Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin International Islamic University (UniSIRAJ), led by its board chairman, Perlis Mufti Datuk Dr Mohd Asri Zainul Abidin.

"The meeting discussed the 2027-2030 Action Plan of the al-Qaradawi Institute of Thought (IPQ), which focuses on research, publications, talent development and strengthening scholarly networks," he said.

Anwar said the meeting also discussed a proposal to organise the International Seminar on al-Qaradawi Thought next year to broaden discourse on Islamic thought and contemporary national governance challenges.
7222a44e4552eb9d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Malaysia is on track to exceed its official full-year gross domestic product (GDP) growth forecast of 4.8 to 5.3 per cent after the economy expanded by 5.5 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, economists said.
The Finance Ministry, in its Economic Outlook 2027 report, raised its 2026 real GDP growth projection to 4.8 to 5.3 per cent, up from 4.0 to 4.5 per cent in Budget 2026.

Prof Dr Yeah Kim Leng, director of the economic studies programme at Sunway University’s Jeffrey Cheah Institute, said third-quarter (Q3) GDP growth of 5.3 per cent affirmed the economy’s resilience despite continuing geopolitical uncertainty and persistent global oil shocks.
“With growth hitting 5.5 per cent in the first three quarters, the economy is on track to exceed the full-year official 4.8-5.3 per cent GDP growth expectation,” he told Bernama.
Yeah said growth moderated slightly from the previous quarter but held up well against a challenging external backdrop marked by geopolitical uncertainty and persistent global oil shocks.

“Encouragingly, the manufacturing sector picked up pace, indicating sustained export demand not only for high-value electronics and optical products but also resource-based chemicals, plastics and rubber products that have higher domestic value added,” he added.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the latest GDP performance was a positive surprise, with growth potentially exceeding the prevailing forecast of 4.8 to 5.3 per cent.
“At 5.3 per cent, the Malaysian economy is seen to be growing above its trend level of around 4.7 per cent,” he said.
Mohd Afzanizam said foreign investors’ positive appetite for Malaysian investments, coupled with stronger demand for technology-related sectors, had helped sustain economic growth.
Full employment also helped support steady consumer spending as inflation remained fairly contained, he added.

Earlier today, the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) said in its advance estimates report that the economy expanded by 5.3 per cent in Q3 2026, following growth of 6.0 per cent in the preceding quarter.
For the first three quarters of 2026, the economy grew by 5.5 per cent, higher than the 4.8 per cent recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.
Domestic demand and E&E to sustain growth

RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB IB) is maintaining its 2026 GDP growth forecast at 5.4 per cent, with its autoregression and leading economic index models pointing to sustained growth of 5.0 to 5.2 per cent in the second half of the year.
“Robust growth of 5.7 per cent in 1H 2026, together with today’s 5.3 per cent growth reading, which was in line with our in-house expectation, reinforces our constructive outlook.
“Looking ahead, economic activity is expected to remain supported by resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in electrical and electronics (E&E) exports,” it said in a research note today.
RHB IB said private consumption was expected to remain firm, supported by healthy labour market conditions, continued income growth and civil servant salary adjustments.
“Private investment should also remain resilient, driven by infrastructure projects, ongoing data centre developments and capacity expansion in manufacturing.

“Meanwhile, continued digitalisation, automation and favourable global demand should encourage further investment, particularly in manufacturing and information and communication technology,” it said.

In a separate note, Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd also maintained its full-year growth forecast at 5.3 per cent, although the stronger-than-expected advance estimate pointed to an upside risk to its projection.
It said any revision would depend on September’s data and the full GDP release.

“Domestic demand should increasingly drive growth in the 2H 2026, backed by resilient consumer spending, strong services activity and continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and digital infrastructure.
“Implementation of approved projects, rising household incomes, and a firm labour market add further support,” it said.

Kenanga said manufacturing should remain a key growth driver, supported by sustained E&E demand linked to AI and data centre expansion, although growth could slow as the effects of front-loading fade.
External risks remain, OPR hold expected
Mohd Afzanizam said the Malaysian economy remained fairly resilient despite external shocks, particularly the ongoing war in Iran, which could affect global supply chains and fuel costs.

He said proactive government measures, such as targeted fuel subsidies through MyKad introduced last year, along with Petroliam Nasional Bhd’s efficiencies in procuring fuel supplies beyond the Strait of Hormuz, had allowed the economy to operate almost seamlessly.
RHB IB, however, said geopolitical tensions in West Asia, commodity price volatility and shifting trade policies posed risks to the outlook.
“Prolonged tensions and elevated oil prices could raise production and transportation costs while dampening global demand,” it said.

Separately, CIMB Treasury and Markets Research said the stronger third-quarter results pointed to a modest overshoot of its 5.0 per cent growth forecast for 2026, which would be revised after the full Q3 GDP release in November.
“Stronger external demand remains supportive of the manufacturing outlook, particularly in E&E, where manufacturers have reported longer order books,” it said.

Despite the stronger GDP growth, CIMB maintained its expectation that Bank Negara Malaysia would keep the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent in November, citing signs of moderating domestic activity and contained inflation.

RHB IB also expects the OPR to remain unchanged at 2.75 per cent at the November Monetary Policy Committee meeting, saying the current economic environment and inflation trajectory support a broadly stable policy outlook.
DOSM said the preliminary GDP report, which provides a detailed and comprehensive analysis of economic performance in Q3 2026, would be released on November 18, 2026. — Bernama
fa650af18483749e: BEIJING: Beijing told White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia on Friday to visit China "more often" after she said the country lacked "proper toilets" less than a week into her new post.

After years of intense rivalry between the United States and China over issues ranging from trade and technology to Taiwan and human rights, the US president's new spokesperson took the relationship between the two sides into uncharted territory.
Zacharia, who previously lived in China and is due to visit next month, recalled in an interview the perception in 2016 that China would soon overtake the United States.

"I remember this very distinctly, having just come from China, thinking, 'How is China the next country on the horizon? They don't even have proper toilets," she told right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec.
In response, China's foreign ministry on Friday suggested she might want to make another trip to the country.
"We welcome her to visit China more often when she has the opportunity," spokeswoman Mao Ning told reporters, suppressing a smile.
Trump has often spoken about his "great relationship" with Chinese President Xi Jinping, whom he has met twice this year, although ties remain strained.

Zacharia's remarks came just days after what many considered a questionable debut before the White House press corps, during which she appeared unable to answer basic questions and at one point referred to her husband as the president.

The 41-year-old is already under scrutiny over her legal credentials after giving an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practising law in the United States.
The self-described lawyer lists herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative non-profit organisation. She has also said she previously worked at a law firm in Beijing.
Asked about her legal background on Thursday, she said she had registered to take the bar exam but was then "distracted and overwhelmed" by plans to move to China with her husband.
Zacharia said she did not retake the bar exam after returning to the United States because of the birth of her first child.
158028da3d1f723d: KUALA LUMPUR: Smartsel Sdn Bhd and Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor), key subsidiaries of Menteri Besar Selangor (Incorporation) (MBI Selangor), will explore the proposed Selangor Dark Fibre Network 2.0, which aims to leverage existing utility corridors to deploy high-capacity fibre networks.
The initiative aims to meet growing connectivity demand from telecommunications operators, data centres, cloud providers, artificial intelligence infrastructure and businesses.

The collaboration between the two subsidiaries was formalised today after the exchange of a memorandum of collaboration (MoC) at the MBI Pavilion during the Selangor International Business Summit (SIBS) 2026.

The partnership combines Air Selangor's water utility infrastructure with Smartsel's digital infrastructure and technology capabilities to develop digital connectivity and intelligent infrastructure across the state.
MBI Selangor group chief executive officer Datuk Ts Saipolyazan M Yusop said the collaboration aimed to translate group synergy into commercial opportunities and greater value for Selangor.

"We must move beyond the traditional mindset of operating as separate companies. We must begin to see ourselves as part of a larger ecosystem, where the assets of one company can create opportunities for another," he said in a statement.

The two companies will also explore smart water technologies, including fibre sensing, Internet of Things (IoT) and real-time monitoring, to strengthen pipeline surveillance, enable earlier leak detection and improve operational efficiency.

The companies will also further assess the potential use of selected elevated water tank and service reservoir sites for telecommunications infrastructure, distributed edge computing and modular data centres, subject to technical feasibility and operational requirements.
"The collaboration will also explore enterprise connectivity, managed information technology, cloud services and cybersecurity to support Air Selangor's digital transformation," the statement said.
Both companies intend to establish a joint working framework to evaluate priority initiatives, assess technical and commercial feasibility, and develop mutually agreed implementation roadmaps.
e833583b47d50fbb: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.
Kids are outsmarting social media bans. That’s not a problem we need to solve.
—Michal Luria, Aliya Bhatia, and Danah Boyd

Social media bans are stacking up. In July, France joined Australia in restricting minors from accessing social media—barring children under 15 from major platforms, before the ban was blocked by the country’s top court on human rights grounds.
The UK aims to forbid kids under 16 from accessing Facebook, TikTok, and other platforms in early 2027, and the EU has announced its own plan to prohibit social media for kids under 15.
But early lessons from Australia, which enacted a ban in 2024, show that these sorts of age restrictions are easily circumvented.
Here’s what we ought to do instead to keep kids safe.
Can’t bear to say goodbye to your pet? Biotech’s got you covered.
—Jessica Hamzelou

I don’t remember much about Peppy, my first and only pet cat. What I do vividly remember, though, is the day she went missing. I was 10 years old, and I searched everywhere for her, scouting nearby fields and woods until sunset. I made posters. We never found her. I was devastated.

Almost 30 years later, pet owners have an expanding set of options to potentially prolong their years with their furry companions. The possibilities include drugs, cloning, and even cryonics. But is that a good thing?

10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch: Form Energy and its iron batteries
Form Energy is one of MIT Technology Review’s 10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch 2026, available exclusively to subscribers.
As wind and solar power grow, utilities need cheaper ways to store electricity for longer periods. Form Energy aims to meet that need with batteries that can store energy for 100 hours.

The company has developed a new type of battery using iron, a far more abundant and cheaper metal than those used in many existing batteries. It uses a process that Form calls “reversible rusting,” in which iron turns to rust as the battery discharges and back to iron when it charges.

One More Thing
SIMON MITCHELL
Inside the experimental world of animal infrastructure

In the mid-2000s, toads were meeting a gruesome end near Ede, a leafy old town in the Netherlands. Residents responded by building wildlife tunnels beneath the road to help them reach their breeding ponds safely.
The crossings became popular. But a few years later, researchers found the local toad population had crashed from more than 10,000 to fewer than 1,000.
The case reflects a wider global push to build wildlife crossings and other forms of “animal infrastructure.” But do they actually help animal populations recover? Read the full story to find out.

4eea087cacb89e15: KOTA BHARU, Oct 16 — Coastal fishermen and aquaculture operators could be hit if El Niño pushes temperatures up to 40°Celsius, prompting calls for early preparations to protect the country’s food production.

Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the phenomenon could drive fish farther out to sea, posing a challenge for coastal fishermen who lack the capacity to fish in deeper waters.
He said the government had discussed preparations for El Niño with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as part of efforts to strengthen national food security.
“Among the measures is an increase in allocations for coastal fishermen; during an El Niño event, temperatures can climb as high as 40 degrees Celsius, which significantly impacts them.

“Fish tend to migrate further offshore, yet coastal fishermen are generally restricted to fishing within a five-nautical-mile radius; they are not equipped to venture further out or fish in deeper waters,” he told reporters after attending the 2026 Kelantan State-level Convention of Parti Amanah Negara here today.

Mohamad said the aquaculture sector could also face challenges if temperatures rise significantly, particularly over the cost of installing protective measures such as canvas covers over fish-rearing ponds.
He said early preparations were crucial to help farmers and other agrifood operators mitigate the effects of hot weather on their activities.
Timely dissemination of information to these groups was also essential to help them take appropriate measures, he added.
Mohamad said the possibility of haze further complicated preparations for the potential impacts of El Niño. — Bernama
50a96646f5715ffe: PASIR GUDANG: A fire involving piles of timber and buoys in Jalan Muhibbah, Kampung Pasir Putih, here, was fully extinguished yesterday after nearly 43 hours of firefighting.
The blaze, which broke out at 10.04pm on Oct 14, engulfed 1.3935ha of open land before firefighters extinguished it at 4.47pm yesterday.

Johor Fire and Rescue Department operations commander Nazarudin Yusof said firefighters had contained 98 per cent of the blaze by 8am yesterday, covering about 148,000 sq ft, before continuing efforts to put out the remaining hotspots.
"By 4.47pm, 100 per cent of the fire had been extinguished, with no remaining area affected by the blaze," he said in a statement today.

A total of 19 firefighters took part in the operation, supported by 17 personnel from other agencies, including the police, Ulu Tiram Volunteer Fire Brigade, Malaysian Civil Defence Force and SWM Environment.

Johor Fire and Rescue Department director Siti Rohani Nadir said witness accounts indicated that several men from a nearby village had set fire to a pile of wood to recover scrap metal, with the blaze believed to have spread to nearby fibreglass floats.
dba278b8a4541d1c: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 16 — Two Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) contractors were critically injured after suffering electric shocks during maintenance work at the utility company’s Kangkar Tebrau main intake substation here this evening.
The incident triggered a fire and disrupted electricity supply in parts of Johor Bahru.
TNB said the fire broke out at 6.03pm, interrupting power supply in several areas around Johor Jaya and its surrounding areas.
“TNB’s technical team has been deployed to the site and is actively working to restore electricity supply to the affected consumers,” the electricity company said in a statement.
The national electricity company also apologised for the inconvenience caused.
The Johor Fire and Rescue Department said the Tebrau fire station received a distress call about the incident at 6.10pm.
“Upon arrival at the scene, the operational response team confirmed that an electrical power outage incident had occurred during maintenance work.

“As a result, two individuals were subjected to electric shock. The team provided initial treatment to both victims before transporting them to the hospital via an Emergency Medical Rescue Services,” said the department spokesman.
The department said firefighters later secured the area before returning to the station.
Earlier, social media users reported blackouts in several parts of Johor Bahru, including Tebrau, Masai and parts of Pasir Gudang.
They also reported that some traffic lights had stopped working, slowing traffic and causing congestion in several locations.
f6f61ba2d06900dc: PESHAWAR: The families of children killed when a school roof collapsed in northwest Pakistan called for "justice" on Friday, a day after more than 30 pupils and a teacher were crushed to death.
A woman teacher and 32 students, mostly younger than 14, died when the building collapsed in the city of Peshawar on Thursday morning.
"The parents of all these children must receive justice," tailor Muhammad Wahab, who lost his 11-year-old nephew Hammad in the accident, told AFP on Friday.
"I appeal to our rulers," he said, adding that Hammad had been "doing well in school" before the tragedy.
Dozens of people gathered outside the school on Friday to mourn the children killed in the collapse, which officials blamed on dilapidated infrastructure.
One grief-stricken father showed AFP a picture on his mobile phone of his young daughter, dressed in red and gold, who lost her life.
Another parent, Asadullah, said he had lost a son, a nephew and three other close relatives in the tragedy.
"The children were good students and often achieved top positions in their classes," he told AFP. "They happily went to school every day."
Residents and rescuers described chaotic scenes in the aftermath of Thursday's collapse, as people scrambled to pull children from beneath the rubble.
A man named Sohail told AFP that "everyone began screaming in panic" when his niece, who had escaped the building, arrived home to tell them it had collapsed.
"When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out," he said.
School owner detained
Images released by emergency services showed rescue workers in high-visibility vests scrambling to move debris, rubble and dirt.
A senior official in Peshawar told AFP that initial reports suggested the roof collapse was due to "weak infrastructure".
"The school owner has been detained," the official said on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak to the media.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed "deep sorrow and grief over the loss of precious lives" in a post on X.
President Asif Ali Zardari described the roof collapse as a "heartbreaking tragedy".
Building collapses are common in Pakistan, largely due to poor safety standards and substandard construction materials in the South Asian nation of more than 240 million people.
In June, more than a dozen children were killed when a roof collapsed at a tutoring centre in the eastern city of Lahore.

c33c998bcf303ec5: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is on track to exceed the official full-year gross domestic product (GDP) growth expectation of 4.8 to 5.3 per cent after the economy expanded by 5.5 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, said economists.
The Finance Ministry, in its Economic Outlook 2027 report, has raised its 2026 real GDP growth projections to 4.8 to 5.3 per cent, up from 4.0 to 4.5 per cent in Budget 2026.

Prof Dr Yeah Kim Leng, director of the economic studies programme at the Jeffrey Cheah Institute of Sunway University, said the third-quarter (3Q) GDP expansion of 5.3 per cent affirms the economy's resilience despite continuing geopolitical uncertainty and persistent global oil shocks.
"With growth hitting 5.5 per cent in the first three quarters, the economy is on track to exceed the full-year official 4.8–5.3 per cent GDP growth expectation," he told Bernama.

Yeah said growth moderated slightly compared with the previous quarter but held up well against the challenging external backdrop of continuing geopolitical uncertainty and persistent global oil shocks.

"Encouragingly, the manufacturing sector picked up pace, indicating sustained export demand not only for high-value electronics and optical products but also resource-based chemicals, plastics and rubber products that have higher domestic value added," he added.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the latest GDP performance was a positive surprise, with growth potentially surprising on the upside against the prevailing projection of between 4.8 per cent and 5.3 per cent.
"At 5.3 per cent, the Malaysian economy is seen to be growing above its trend level of around 4.7 per cent," he said.
Mohd Afzanizam said positive appetite among foreign investors to invest in Malaysia, along with greater demand for the technology-related sector, helped sustain economic growth momentum.
Full employment also helped maintain steady consumer spending as inflation remained fairly contained, he added.

Earlier today, the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) announced in its advanced estimates report that Malaysia's economy expanded by 5.3 per cent in 3Q 2026, after registering 6.0 per cent growth in the preceding quarter, while for the first three quarters of 2026, the economy achieved growth of 5.5 per cent, higher than the 4.8 per cent recorded in 2025's corresponding period.
Domestic demand and E&E to sustain growth

Meanwhile, RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB IB) is maintaining its 2026 GDP growth projection at 5.4 per cent, with its autoregression and leading economic index models pointing to sustained growth momentum of 5.0–5.2 per cent in the second half of the year (2H 2026).
"Robust growth of 5.7 per cent in 1H 2026, together with today's 5.3 per cent growth reading, which was in line with our in-house expectation, reinforces our constructive outlook.
"Looking ahead, economic activity is expected to remain supported by resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in electrical and electronics (E&E) exports," it said in a research note today.
RHB IB said private consumption is projected to remain firm, underpinned by healthy labour market conditions, continued income growth and civil servant salary adjustments.
"Private investment should also remain resilient, driven by infrastructure projects, ongoing data centre developments and capacity expansion in manufacturing.

"Meanwhile, continued digitalisation, automation and favourable global demand should encourage further investment, particularly in manufacturing and information and communication technology," it said.

In a separate note, Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd has also maintained its full-year growth forecast at 5.3 per cent, although the stronger-than-expected advance estimate points to an upside risk to its forecast.
It said any revision would hinge on September's data and the full GDP release.

"Domestic demand should increasingly drive growth in the 2H 2026, backed by resilient consumer spending, strong services activity and continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and digital infrastructure.
"Implementation of approved projects, rising household incomes, and a firm labour market add further support," it said.
Kenanga said that manufacturing should remain a key driver on sustained E&E demand from AI and data centre expansion, although growth may slow as front-loading fades.
External risks remain, OPR hold expected
Mohd Afzanizam said the Malaysian economy remained fairly resilient despite external shocks, especially the ongoing war in Iran, which is likely to affect global supply chains and fuel costs.

He said proactive government measures, such as targeted fuel subsidies via MyKad since last year, along with efficiencies demonstrated by Petroliam Nasional Bhd in procuring fuel supplies beyond the Strait of Hormuz, had allowed the economy to operate almost seamlessly.
RHB IB, however, said geopolitical tensions in West Asia, commodity price volatility and shifting trade policies pose risks to the outlook.
"Prolonged tensions and elevated oil prices could raise production and transportation costs while dampening global demand," it said.

Separately, CIMB Treasury and Markets Research said the stronger third-quarter outturn points to a modest overshoot of its 5.0 per cent growth forecast for 2026, which would be revised after the full 3Q GDP release in November.
"Stronger external demand remains supportive of the manufacturing outlook, particularly in E&E, where manufacturers have reported longer order books," it said.

Despite the GDP upside, CIMB retained its expectation for Bank Negara Malaysia to hold the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent in November, given signs of moderating domestic activity and contained inflation.

RHB IB also expects the OPR to remain unchanged at 2.75 per cent at the November Monetary Policy Committee meeting, saying the current economic environment and inflation trajectory support a broadly stable policy outlook.
DOSM said the preliminary GDP, which provides a detailed and comprehensive analysis of economic performance for 3Q 2026, will be released on Nov 18, 2026.

e9e9a3d52fd23433: OCTOBER 16 — Anyone who has spent time in manufacturing knows that even the best-laid plans can change overnight.
A supplier revises its prices, a shipment arrives late, or a customer changes an order at short notice, leaving the production team to work out how best to keep things moving.
For Malaysian manufacturers, these everyday realities now sit alongside shifting trade policies, geopolitical tensions and changing customer expectations.
It is understandable that business leaders are keeping a close eye on what might happen next.
But there is another question worth asking: how well do we understand what is happening within our own businesses today?
Malaysia’s manufacturing sector generated RM1.97 trillion in sales in 2025, up 4.2 per cent from the previous year, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM).
With 2.4 million people employed in the sector, there is plenty of reason to be optimistic about its contribution to the economy.
The opportunity now is to build on that foundation by helping manufacturers make confident decisions, even when conditions are less predictable.
The value of knowing where you stand
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

A worker operates machinery on a manufacturing production line in Malaysia, where manufacturers face pressure to improve productivity, manage costs and respond to changing market conditions. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
For manufacturers serving overseas markets, developments thousands of kilometres away can have very real consequences on the factory floor.
A change in demand can alter order volumes, higher freight costs can eat into margins, and a delayed component can hold up an entire production run.
Of course, no business can control everything happening around it. What it can do, however, is get a clearer view of how these changes affect its operations.

Take a new customer order, for instance. The revenue might look attractive, but can the factory accommodate it without disrupting existing commitments? Are the necessary materials available, and do the original cost estimates still hold?
These are straightforward questions, yet answering them can be surprisingly difficult when information about inventory, production, purchasing and finances sits in different places.
When teams have a shared, up-to-date picture of the business, these conversations become much easier.
Managers can spot potential constraints earlier, explore alternatives and make decisions based on what is actually happening, rather than what they assume is happening.
That does not remove the uncertainty, but it does give businesses more room to respond thoughtfully.
Busy does not always mean better
One thing worth remembering is that growth and profitability do not always move in tandem.
A factory can be running at full capacity while some jobs deliver thinner margins than expected, or an increase in orders can leave too much cash tied up in inventory.
For business leaders, the question is not simply how to secure more orders, but how to make sure those orders contribute to a healthier business.

Having a clearer view of costs and margins by product, customer or job can help management decide which opportunities make commercial sense, where efficiencies might be found and when pricing arrangements need another look.
Monthly reports remain useful, but business rarely waits for the end of the month.
When costs change or a delivery is delayed, being able to understand the implications promptly can make a meaningful difference to the decisions that follow.
Better decisions start with a shared picture
Production needs to know what can realistically be delivered, purchasing needs to understand supplier availability, and finance needs to see how decisions affect costs and cash flow.
These priorities are connected, yet teams can easily end up working with different versions of the same picture.
When information flows across the business, teams can spend less time reconciling numbers and more time deciding what to do next.
A potential delay becomes a chance to explore alternatives early, while a change in material costs can prompt a timely conversation about pricing.
The value lies not simply in having better information, but in giving people the context to act on it.
Confidence comes from being prepared
For Malaysian manufacturers, opportunities remain to explore new markets, improve productivity and move into higher-value activities.
Making the most of them does not require a perfect forecast, but it does require an honest understanding of what the business can deliver and where it can improve.
Unexpected changes will always be part of manufacturing. What matters is how quickly businesses recognise them, understand their implications and respond.

That hinges on having a clear view of increasingly complex, interconnected operations, so manufacturers can make better decisions, improve productivity and move up the value chain in line with the ambitions of Malaysia’s New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP) 2030.

84ec2b3b3bf2826e: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Air Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has urged the operator of Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Port (STOLport) in Miri, Sarawak, to review its rescue and firefighting arrangements after a helicopter crash killed five people, including four Health Ministry personnel, on September 8.

The AAIB recommended that aerodrome operator Malaysia Airports Sdn Bhd (MASB) review rescue and firefighting arrangements across its STOLports to ensure auxiliary personnel were properly trained and equipped, and that firefighting equipment and personal protective equipment (PPE) were properly maintained and serviceable.

The bureau said the recommendation followed findings that Malaysia Volunteers Corps Department (Rela) personnel assigned to auxiliary rescue and firefighting duties had responded to the blaze without appropriate firefighting PPE.

“Some of the available PPE exhibited visible signs of deterioration and damage, which could adversely affect the safety and effectiveness of the emergency response,” the AAIB said in its preliminary report.

The report said 12 dry powder fire extinguishers at the STOLport terminal were used by responders and local villagers in an attempt to put out the flames, but the fire continued to burn for several hours.
All five occupants on board – a 30-year-old Malaysian pilot and four Health Ministry personnel – died from severe burn injuries, according to post-mortem findings cited in the report.

The Messerschmitt-Bölkow-Blohm BO105 S helicopter, registered as 9M-LLF and operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd under the callsign MEDIC3, was conducting a scheduled Flying Doctor Service flight.

The aircraft is designed for various operations, including passenger transport, utility work, medical evacuation and other specialised missions, with a maximum take-off mass of about 2,500kg, depending on its configuration.

The report said a 37-second ground-based video captured the helicopter’s final moments, showing it in flight with a visible smoke trail and apparent flames behind the main gearbox as it approached Runway 04.
The helicopter came to rest about 25 metres from the runway threshold and was destroyed by fire.
All communication frequencies were operating normally, and no emergency call or distress transmission from the helicopter was recorded between departure and the crash, the report said.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department found that weather conditions near Long Lellang STOLport were generally good, with horizontal visibility exceeding 10km during the period assessed.
As an immediate safety measure, Layang-Layang Aerospace suspended operations of aircraft fitted with the same engine type pending airworthiness verification.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia cleared the affected aircraft to return to service on September 13 after technical reviews, the report said.

A detailed examination of the wreckage will be conducted to establish the nature and extent of the damage and, where possible, the sequence and development of the fire and ground-contact damage. The findings will be included in the final report.

The Transport Ministry said information in the preliminary report could be revised as additional evidence emerged, while a comprehensive analysis and the investigation’s conclusions would be presented in the final report.
The ministry said the investigation was intended to prevent similar accidents from recurring, rather than determine fault or liability.

“The ministry appreciates the efforts of the AAIB and the cooperation of all parties involved in assisting the investigation, and remains committed to strengthening the country’s aviation safety,” it said. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Rela stands for Jabatan Sukarelawan Malaysia, or the Malaysia Volunteers Corps Department in English.
4f9591a466804ba8: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian is suspected of masterminding an agarwood investment scam involving more than HK$14 million (RM7.2 million) that was uncovered by Hong Kong police on Wednesday.
The South China Morning Post reported that the man was among six people arrested in raids across Hong Kong. The other five suspects were Hong Kong residents.
The operation, codenamed "Shadow Net", was launched by the Hong Kong Police Commercial Crime Bureau after it received 21 reports from investors since September.
Commercial Crime Bureau Superintendent Allan Chu Ming-lun said most victims were aged between 52 and 82.
He said they had invested between HK$30,000 (RM15,565) and HK$1.9 million (RM985,800) in schemes offered by a Hong Kong-based company since 2017.
The company claimed to have offices in Malaysia, Singapore, New York and Hong Kong, as well as large agarwood plantations in Malaysia producing essential oils, tea and food.
"Key members of the syndicate took investors on visits to agarwood plantations in Malaysia to gain their confidence.
"The company also frequently organised investment seminars at its Hong Kong office, offering free tours and meals to encourage existing members to recruit new investors," he said as quoted by SCMP.
Investigations found that the company offered at least four investment schemes promising high returns.
Under one scheme, investors could buy an agarwood tree for HK$10,000 (RM5,194) in return for promised monthly payouts of HK$300 (RM156), equivalent to 36 per cent annually.
They were also promised a full refund after three years, while the monthly returns were recorded as reward points on the company's mobile application.
However, some investors began finding in 2024 that they could neither withdraw their returns nor recover their initial investments.
Chu said the company then used various excuses to delay payments and introduced new schemes to persuade investors to transfer their funds from earlier investments.

In 2025, it launched an intellectual property licensing scheme promising annual returns of up to 25 per cent. Investors unable to recover their money from earlier schemes eventually transferred their funds into the new investment.
Earlier this year, the company introduced a cryptocurrency called IBBB Coin, claiming its value would rise through the tokenisation of agarwood trees.
However, the cryptocurrency has since lost more than 99 per cent of its value, leaving buyers' holdings almost worthless, Chu said.
The company also offered an investment scheme involving automated car wash centres in mainland China, promising annual returns of 30 per cent.
During the operation, police searched the company's office and warehouse in Kwun Tong, as well as the homes of the suspects.
Police seized about HK$540,000 in cash, 25 mobile phones, computers, investment contracts and products suspected to contain agarwood.
They are examining the seized electronic devices and contacting other potential victims for further information.
On Oct 14, Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission placed the company on its alert list for suspicious investment products.

65b644b9abf977c8: BRUSSELS: EU leaders grappled Friday with how to tackle Ukraine's dependence on Starlink satellite communications supporting its battlefield operations, as Kyiv was rocked by disruptions to the US-owned system.

The bloc's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Europe did not have a readily available alternative to technology controlled by Elon Musk's SpaceX, as she arrived at an EU summit where the issue will be high on the agenda.

"Starlink is really necessary for Ukraine and unfortunately in (the) short term Europe can't replace this capability," Kallas said before the talks, where Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky was also in attendance.
Ukraine uses Starshield, Starlink's military-grade satellite service, for its battlefield communications, mid-range strikes on Russian-occupied territory and interceptor drones.
It also uses SpaceX's parallel Starlink civilian satellite system, but not for offensive operations.
Musk has shifted stance on Ukraine several times since Russia's invasion in 2022.
Kyiv reported restrictions on its use of the Starlink system this week. Musk said any disruption was the responsibility of the US government, not his SpaceX firm.
Kallas said the European Defence Agency had mapped all the "critical capabilities" that Europe was missing and needed to fulfil, adding Europe needed to fill these gaps "as soon as possible".
European leaders echoed the urgency for Europe to build its capacities.
"Starlink is the key for Ukraine actually to fight or fight back," Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs told reporters.
"It takes time for us to have the same capabilities. We do have, but not enough. So this is strategically something we have to discuss today."
Zelensky was taking part in the leaders' talks with Ukraine and Europe's own security and defence on the agenda.

Also addressing the Starlink issue, Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said he had discussed with French President Emmanuel Macron Thursday "how we, as Europeans, can provide more of these kinds of services in the not too distant future".

Speeds were slower on the system on Wednesday, affecting connectivity, according to Ukrainian officials, who have suggested Washington was behind slower speeds reported on some Starlink internet terminals.
British defence minister Wes Streeting also said he discussed Starlink with his US counterpart Pete Hegseth Thursday.

"It's not yet clear to us in the UK what happened, why the service interruption occurred. But I am reassured, and was reassured directly by Secretary Hegseth, that the service has been restored," he told the BBC Friday.
16bbd6def5a45c1b: KUALA LUMPUR: Actress Datin Intan Najuwa is set to take legal action against an individual who sent her death threats using a fake social media account.
In a recent post, Intan, whose full name is Intan Najuwa Abdul Wahid, revealed that the harasser had resurfaced after months of silence.
She confirmed that the person behind the account is a man, adding that he used to send her direct messages (DMs) almost daily, as well as harassing her friends and calling her club.
"Today (yesterday), he reappeared after months of silence. Previously, he would harass me almost every day via DMs," the 29-year-old artiste wrote on her Instagram Story.

"It wasn't just me—he also sent DMs and emails to all my friends. He even went as far as calling the Kuala Lumpur Polo Club office almost daily, just to look for me, insisting on speaking to me, and threatening me with various things."
The situation escalated when the man began leaving comments containing explicit death threats.
"The person behind this fake account is a man. He has resurfaced, but this time with comments threatening to kill me," she said.
"To whoever is behind this fake account, please stop this behaviour immediately. I can no longer tolerate the harassment, threats, and invasion of privacy that you have been carrying out."
Issuing a stern warning, the actress emphasised that death threats and persistent harassment are serious matters.
She intends to pursue legal action if the individual does not stop immediately.

"If I file a police report and initiate legal proceedings, you could face severe legal consequences," Intan warned. "I have every right to protect my own safety, my privacy, and my family. This must stop."
This is not the first time the actress has faced online abuse. She previously lodged a police report after an individual targeted her with baseless accusations.
844587f3507926c3: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The ringgit closed higher against the US dollar on Friday, supported by Malaysia’s higher-than-expected advance GDP estimate for the third quarter of 2026 (3Q 2026).
At 6pm, the ringgit rose to 4.0795/0835 against the greenback from Thursday’s close of 4.0800/0835.

Earlier today, the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), in its Advance GDP Estimates for 3Q 2026 report, said the economy expanded by 5.3 per cent in the third quarter, after registering 6.0 per cent growth in the preceding quarter.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam told Bernama that the latest announcement suggests that the Malaysian economy remains fairly resilient.

“It would not be a surprise if the whole-year GDP comes in higher than the current projection of 4.8 per cent to 5.3 per cent, with the nine months of 2026 (9M 2026) GDP growth already at 5.5 per cent.
“We sense that the anticipation for a normalisation in Overnight Policy Rate (from the pre-emptive cut in July 2025) would gather pace in light of the current growth trajectory,” he said.
At the close, the ringgit traded mostly lower against a basket of major currencies.

It increased against the Japanese yen to 2.5831/5895 from 2.5869/5892 at Thursday’s close but decreased against the euro to 4.5911/5956from 4.5761/5801 and inched down against the British pound to 5.4396/4449 from 5.4101/4147.
Against its ASEAN peers, the local note gained against the Indonesian rupiah to 226.3/226.6 from 227.4/227.7 and edged down against the Philippine peso at 6.48/6.49 from 6.47/6.48.
It was lower against the Singapore dollar to 3.1889/1922 from 3.1818/1848 at yesterday’s close and decreased against the Thai baht to 12.2101/2268 from 12.1758/1914. — Bernama
54fec28b17ec1a7b: PESHAWAR: The families of children killed in a roof collapse at a school in northwest Pakistan called for "justice" on Friday, the day after more than 30 pupils and a teacher were crushed to death.
A woman teacher and 32 students, mostly younger than 14, died in the building collapse in the city of Peshawar on Thursday morning.
"The parents of all these children must receive justice," tailor Muhammad Wahab, who lost his 11-year-old nephew Hammad in the accident, told AFP on Friday.
"I appeal to our rulers," he said, adding that Hammad had been "doing well in school" before the tragedy.
Dozens of people gathered on Friday outside the school to mourn the children who were killed in the collapse, which officials blamed on dilapidated infrastructure.
One grief-stricken father showed AFP a picture on his mobile phone of his young daughter, dressed in red and gold, who lost her life.
Another parent, Asadullah, said he lost a son, nephew, and three other close relatives in the tragedy.
"The children were good students and often achieved top positions in their classes," he told AFP. "They happily went to school every day".
Residents and rescuers described chaotic scenes in the aftermath of Thursday's collapse, as people scrambled to pull children out from under the rubble.
A man named Sohail told AFP that "everyone began screaming in panic" when his niece, who had escaped the building, arrived home to tell them it had collapsed.
"When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out," he said.
School owner detained
Images released by emergency services showed rescue workers in high-visibility vests scrambling to move debris, rubble and dirt.
A senior official in Peshawar told AFP that initial reports suggested the roof collapse was due to "weak infrastructure".
"The school owner has been detained," the official said on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to talk to the media.
Prime minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed "deep sorrow and grief over the loss of precious lives" in an X post.
President Asif Ali Zardari described the roof collapse as a "heartbreaking tragedy".
Building collapses are common in Pakistan, largely due to poor safety standards and substandard construction materials in the South Asian nation of more than 240 million people.
In June, more than a dozen children were killed when a roof collapsed at a tutoring centre in the eastern city of Lahore.
In 2025, 27 people were killed and 10 injured when a five-storey building collapsed in the impoverished Lyari area of the southern city of Karachi.

Bantuan itu disampaikan pada 9 Okt lepas di Dewan Sultan Mizan, Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) di Kuala Nerus, Terengganu.

cbc1d3af27779a8d: KUALA LUMPUR: Unicef, the United Nations children’s fund, has called for stronger measures to protect children from the health and social impacts of the recurring haze crisis, including ensuring access to healthcare, education and essential support during school closures.

In a statement today, Unicef Malaysia deputy representative Sanja Saranovic said about nine in 10 of Malaysia’s nine million children are exposed to harmful fine particulate matter (PM2.5), which can penetrate deep into the lungs and bloodstream, potentially causing serious health problems.

“Children are particularly vulnerable to air pollution because their lungs, brains and immune systems are still developing, with exposure potentially causing damage that could begin before birth and last a lifetime,” she said.

Saranovic outlined four priorities to strengthen protection during haze episodes. These were: helping families prepare, ensuring continuity of learning, maintaining access to healthcare and social support, and strengthening preparedness plans at schools and clinics.

She said families should receive clear information on school closures and practical advice on reducing exposure to polluted air, while schools should provide offline learning materials and self-learning kits for children without devices or reliable internet access.

Schools and healthcare facilities should have haze preparedness plans linked to official air-quality information and health guidance, with low-cost air-quality monitors helping schools assess local conditions and respond accordingly.

“In haze hotspots, air purifiers in schools can also be considered as part of a targeted strategy, recognising the costs and the need to prioritise schools and children facing the greatest exposure,” she said.

Saranovic acknowledged the need for school closures to safeguard children from poor air quality. However, prolonged disruptions could affect their learning and well-being, particularly those without devices or reliable internet access for home-based learning, she said. Schools also served as places where children could access daily routines, trusted adults, peer connections and, in some cases, vital meals and social support.

Tackling the haze crisis required collective action by Malaysia and its neighbours to prevent forest and peatland fires, strengthen air-quality monitoring and ensure greater accountability among governments and businesses, while safeguarding the livelihoods of affected communities, Saranovic said.
“Children cannot stop the fires, clear the air, or decide when schools will reopen. They depend on adults to act, and they have a right to be heard in those decisions,” she said.
ecf8f66c43d8420d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Air quality in Larkin and Pasir Gudang, Johor, deteriorated to very unhealthy levels this evening, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaching 202 as at 5.30pm, while 27 other areas nationwide recorded unhealthy readings.

According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, six other areas in Johor recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Pengerang (181), Batu Pahat and Kota Tinggi (171 each), Kluang (168), Tangkak (159) and Segamat (156).
In Selangor, Johan Setia recorded the highest reading at 184, followed by Klang (176), Petaling Jaya (173), Shah Alam (168), Banting (162) and Kuala Selangor (152).
Three stations in Negeri Sembilan also recorded unhealthy readings: Nilai (181), Seremban (174) and Port Dickson (170).
In Melaka, Bandaraya Melaka recorded an API of 180, followed by Bukit Rambai (175) and Alor Gajah (169).
In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda and Cheras both recorded an API of 163, while Putrajaya registered 170.
Unhealthy air quality was also reported in Perak at Seri Manjung (160) and Tanjung Malim (158); in Pahang at Temerloh (139) and Rompin (103); and in Sabah at Tawau (153) and Sandakan (107).
Across the country, 27 areas recorded moderate API readings, while Sarikei in Sarawak was the only station with good air quality, at 50.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy; and above 300, hazardous. — Bernama
6bb73cf68a3a4247: SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — A lorry carrying dry food products lost control and crashed into a Road Transport Department (JPJ) car and another lorry during a roadside inspection, killing a JPJ officer and injuring three others on the North-South Expressway near Senawang, police said today.

Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the two JPJ personnel had been inspecting a motoloader carrying a cabin load on the emergency lane at Kilometre 256.1 northbound when the lorry approached from behind at about 10.30pm yesterday.
“However, the lorry lost control and failed to avoid the vehicles, crashing into the rear of the JPJ car and the motoloader,” he said in a statement.
The 42-year-old JPJ officer suffered head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.
His 32-year-old colleague sustained serious head injuries and injuries to several parts of his body and was receiving treatment at Tuanku Ja’afar Seremban Hospital.
The two lorry drivers, aged 44 and 48, also suffered injuries to their legs and bodies and were receiving treatment at the hospital’s emergency department.
Alzafny said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He urged anyone with information about the crash to contact investigating officer Inspector Syakinah Ahmad at 06-6033394 or visit the nearest police station to assist with investigations.

* Editor’s note: JPJ stands for Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan in Malay, or the Road Transport Department in English. PLUS is the Malay abbreviation for Projek Lebuhraya Utara-Selatan, the operator of the North-South Expressway.
f834a99ab273462e: JOHOR BARU: A 67-year-old man was found dead with head injuries after being repeatedly beaten with a blunt object in Permas Jaya, here, yesterday.
Johor Baru (Selatan) deputy police chief Superintendent Ng Swie Chait said the victim also suffered injuries to his face and arms.
He said police received a report from the public at 4.54pm before tracking down and arresting a 47-year-old man believed to have been involved in the murder.
The suspect was arrested outside an eatery in Bandar Baru Permas Jaya at 6pm.
Ng said police seized an iron walking stick and a framed portrait to assist investigations.
"Checks found that the suspect has a criminal record with two entries, including one for a drug-related offence. However, a urine test came back negative for drug abuse," he said in a statement.
The suspect has been remanded for seven days from today to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
A post-mortem examination at Sultan Ismail Hospital today found that the cause of death was multiple blunt-force trauma to the head.
Police urged anyone with information on the incident to contact the district police headquarters at 07-2182323.
cc7db2c67b674cbb: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Union of Bank Employees (NUBE) failed in its appeal against a cease and desist order to refrain from making public statements and organising pickets over a trade dispute with Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank).
High Court judge Norliza Othman dismissed the appeal today with RM10,000 in costs.
In her broad grounds, Norliza said the order, handed down by the Industrial Court, was not an injunction of the kind granted by civil courts under the Specific Relief Act 1950.
The Industrial Court did not have the jurisdiction to issue such an injunction, she said.
Instead, it was an ancillary order made under Sections 28 and 29(g) of the Industrial Relations Act 1967 to preserve the status quo, prevent escalation, and ensure orderly proceedings.
The restraint was also intended to prevent a trial by media while the trade dispute remained unresolved, and to protect the integrity of the Industrial Court's proceedings.
Norliza agreed that denying the Industrial Court the power to maintain order in its proceedings would undermine the objectives of the law and reduce it to a “toothless tiger”.
She also rejected NUBE's contention that the order had prejudged the dispute, stressing that it was an interim order and no findings had been made on the merits of the allegations against Maybank.
On freedom of speech under Article 10 of the Federal Constitution, Norliza said the right was not absolute and could be restricted.
She agreed that the union's public postings and pickets concerned the very subject matter before the Industrial Court and risked undermining the proceedings.
The restraint was necessary to ensure the dispute could be fairly heard and determined, she said.
The dispute arose from a sexual harassment allegation made by a former employee of the bank against a colleague.
Although the matter was addressed in 2021, it resurfaced in 2024 during an unrelated grievance process, leading to public campaigns and pickets by NUBE.
The union continued its actions after the dispute was referred to the Industrial Court, prompting Maybank to seek interim relief under Sections 29(g) and 30 of the Act.
Janice Anne Leo, Chong Jen Hui and Adrienne Sena appeared for Maybank, while Ravi Nekoo and Arvinkumar Mohan represented NUBE.
728c5c6d133c5aed: BAGDHAD: Iraq's prime minister completed his cabinet line-up by appointing a US-designated terrorist after receiving Washington's approval, in a bid to advance efforts to disarm Iran-backed groups in the country, diplomatic sources told AFP.
On Thursday night, Ali al-Zaidi announced the completion of his government, appointing Laith al-Khazali, a senior leader in the US-blacklisted Asaib Ahl al-Haq group, as one of his deputies.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi "secured tacit US approval during his visit to the US in September" for the UN General Assembly, and during which he met President Donald Trump, a diplomatic source said on Friday.

The US agreed to the participation of some pro-Iran factions in the government "after the prime minister promised to move forward with his disarmament plans and provided guarantees that the groups will not attack US interests in Iraq", the source added.
The US, which wields significant influence in Iraq, "wants to help him advance his plans".
Khazali and his brother Qais, the leader of Asaib Ahl al-Haq, are both designated as "global terrorists" by Washington, which sees them as "violent proxies" of Iran.
But their group has emerged as a major political force, winning 27 seats in the latest parliamentary elections.
It was among the first to back Zaidi's plan to bring all arms under state control, says it has begun handing over its own weapons, and has not been publicly linked to recent attacks on US interests.

Washington accuses the Khazali brothers, both former US detainees, of attacks on its forces after the 2003 invasion of Iraq, including a 2007 attack that led to the capture and killing of five American soldiers.
A second diplomatic source confirmed that the US had given Zaidi the green light to complete his government with the participation of some factions.
One such faction, the Iran-backed Kataeb Sayyid al-Shuhada, part of the Islamic Resistance in Iraq that has recently claimed hundreds of attacks on US interests, secured the tourism ministry.
The US has previously turned a blind eye to the participation of some blacklisted factions in Iraqi governments.

But, this time the shift came after months of mounting pressure on Zaidi to disarm Iran-backed groups, which have long targeted US interests in Iraq and stepped up their attacks during the Middle East war in support of Tehran.

"Things changed," the first diplomatic source said, adding that the US had already shown in Syria its willingness to shift tactics, with its support for Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, who was previously designated a terrorist.

Zaidi, who assumed office earlier this year with US blessing, initially set Sept 30, the date marking the end of the US-led coalition mission in Iraq, as the deadline for factions to hand over their weapons.
He later withdrew it as talks continued, and then set a new deadline of June 30.
Zaidi announced part of his cabinet in May, but the remaining portfolios were held up by negotiations among political parties, including demands from some factions for government representation.

867e5823014dc3e5: PETALING JAYA: The family of the late Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42, lodged a police report against Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus here today over his remarks on the death of the detainee.

Lawyer Latheefa Koya said the report was prompted by Fadil's statements on Noorizwan's death, which she described as dishonest and an attempt to justify the incident on the grounds that the deceased had a criminal record.
"We were shocked by the statements made during yesterday's press conference because they contradicted what we had witnessed ourselves.
"This was particularly evident from our meeting with pathologist Dr Faridah on Monday, Oct 12, at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM).
"During the meeting, Dr Faridah briefed us and explained the autopsy findings, supported by photographic evidence of the injuries sustained by the deceased.

"However, the way Datuk Fadil delivered his statements at the press conference gave the impression that he was completely unaware of the pathologist's briefing and findings," she said at a press conference at the Lawyers for Liberty (LFL) office here today.
She said officers from the federal custodial death investigation unit were also present at the meeting.

Earlier, Latheefa, fellow lawyer N. Surendran, Noorizwan's brother Nooranis Zulkefly and several family members went to the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters to lodge the report at about 3pm.
In the report, Latheefa said Fadil's statements at the press conference had failed to address the severe injuries found on Noorizwan's body, as documented in the forensic findings.
"The Kuala Lumpur police chief did not mention that there were severe injuries on Noorizwan's body, despite this being a finding by the pathologist.
"He also claimed that the cause of death had yet to be finalised, although the pathologist had already informed the police and the family of the cause," she said in the report.

Latheefa said Fadil's statements were inaccurate and misleading, adding that his position as Kuala Lumpur police chief presented a conflict of interest because the case involved personnel under his command.

She said the federal police should conduct the investigation under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which deals with murder, and that the personnel involved should only be allowed to return to duty if no criminal elements were found.
Yesterday, the media reported that police were awaiting the full report from the Chemistry Department and the pathology findings to determine the cause of death of a man who died in custody on Oct 1.
Fadil was reported to have said that the detainee, a local man in his 40s, died at 1.52am while receiving treatment at HCTM.
58260bb4b36bfe8b: PETALING JAYA: Men’s doubles shuttlers Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik have qualified for the semi-finals of the Denmark Open, setting up a highly anticipated clash with South Korea’s world No 1 Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae for a place in the final.

In today’s quarter-final, the Malaysian world No 4 pair stamped their superiority over Japan’s Hiroki Okamura-Kyohei Yamashita, winning comfortably 21-16, 21-18 in 37 minutes at the SJF Bank Arena in Odense.
Aaron-Wooi Yik, who reunited for the World Tour Super 750 tournament after a brief split to try new combinations, last beat the South Koreans in the Asian Games semi-final last month.
However, Won Ho-Seung Jae have beaten Aaron-Wooi Yik three times in their five encounters todate.

Aaron-Wooi Yik are still looking for their first World Tour title this year after finishing as runners-up in three top-tier tournaments - the Malaysia Open, the All England, and the World Championships.

Aaron was also a runner-up at the Taipei Open when he partnered Aaron Tai as part of the Badminton Association of Malaysia's experiment to find the best combinations for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
