f95fdf3ccf426d2e: ARAU: Tindakan penguatkuasaan Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) Perlis menyumbang kepada pemulihan hasil melalui nilai lucut hak berjumlah RM698,255.55 sepanjang tempoh 2024 hingga tahun ini.
Pengarah SPRM Perlis Mohd Nor Adha Ab Gani berkata, sepanjang tempoh itu, pihaknya turut membuka 65 kertas siasatan selain merekodkan 84 tangkapan dan 37 tuduhan di mahkamah.

“Sebanyak 20 kertas siasatan dibuka pada 2024 melibatkan 27 tangkapan dan 13 tuduhan dengan nilai lucut hak RM323,872.55 manakala pada tahun lepas, 22 kertas siasatan dibuka membabitkan 34 tangkapan dan 16 tuduhan, dengan nilai lucut hak RM374,168.

“Setakat Januari lepas hingga kini pula, SPRM Perlis membuka 23 kertas siasatan melibatkan 23 tangkapan dan lapan tuduhan dengan nilai lucut hak RM215,” katanya dalam kenyataan yang dikeluarkan Istana Arau hari ini.
Menurut kenyataan itu, perkara berkenaan dipersembahkan Mohd Nor Adha kepada Raja Muda Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail dalam satu majlis perpisahan di Istana Arau baru-baru ini.

Mohd Nor Adha berkata, SPRM Perlis turut memberi penekanan terhadap aspek pencegahan melalui pengemukaan 61 Syor Penambahbaikan Tatakelola kepada jabatan dan badan berkanun pada peringkat persekutuan serta negeri.
“Usaha ini bertujuan memperkukuh sistem penyampaian perkhidmatan awam, meningkatkan integriti organisasi serta menutup ruang dan peluang berlakunya rasuah,” katanya.
Beliau berkata, komitmen dan kecemerlangan warga SPRM Perlis turut mendapat pengiktirafan menerusi beberapa anugerah, antaranya Anugerah Khas Ketua Pesuruhjaya pada 2024 dan 2025.

Mohd Nor Adha berkata, SPRM Perlis turut meraih Anugerah Pengurusan KPI Terbaik 2025 dengan markah penilaian sebanyak 97.45%, selain memperoleh tempat ketiga bagi Anugerah Pengurusan Kewangan Terbaik 2025.

“Pencapaian tersebut membuktikan kesungguhan SPRM Perlis dalam mengimbangi tindakan penguatkuasaan dengan langkah pencegahan secara berterusan demi membentuk persekitaran pentadbiran yang berintegriti, telus dan bertanggungjawab,” katanya.

Menurut kenyataan itu, pada majlis berkenaan, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra menzahirkan penghargaan dan ucapan terima kasih kepada Mohd Nor Adha atas khidmat bakti serta komitmen beliau dalam menerajui SPRM Perlis sepanjang tempoh dua tahun tujuh bulan bermula 1 Mac 2024 hingga esok.
Baginda turut mengucapkan tahniah atas kenaikan pangkat beliau dan pelantikan sebagai pengarah SPRM Terengganu yang berkuat kuasa 18 Okt ini.

Raja Muda Perlis berharap pengalaman yang ditunjukkan sepanjang berkhidmat di Perlis akan menjadi bekalan berharga untuk meneruskan tanggungjawab baharu, di samping mengekalkan komitmen dalam memperkukuh integriti, tatakelola dan usaha membanteras rasuah demi kepentingan negara.
b759b83f6f5f588b: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 16 — Five Malaysians arrested for concealing five kilograms of cocaine in their shoe soles at Haneda International Airport in Tokyo, Japan, on October 10 are believed to have been drug mules paid RM8,000 each.

Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the suspects, aged between 19 and 26, were each given the shoes by a drug syndicate that is still being identified.
“We believe they (the suspects) were aware of what they were carrying, which is an illegal substance,” he told a press conference at the Johor Contingent Police Headquarters here today.
He said police were investigating whether all the suspects were directly involved in the syndicate and whether they had previously travelled to other countries using the same modus operandi.
He added that initial checks showed none of the five suspects had a criminal record.
Hussein said all the suspects, including a married couple, were believed to have travelled to Japan for a holiday before being detained by the authorities.
“The group was led by the woman’s husband, and she invited her friends for a trip to Japan, with each given a pair of shoes that had been pre-stuffed with drugs,” he said.
He said another Malaysian, who was not arrested in connection with the case, was a travel agent and had been cleared of involvement.
Hussein previously said checks confirmed that the group had departed from Terminal 2 of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
Japanese customs authorities found the drugs inside the shoe soles worn by all the suspects.
He said the NCID had sent a team to Japan to investigate and gather details of the case.
On the drug seizure in Laos, he confirmed that the illicit substances transported on a private jet had been ordered by two Filipino nationals.
He said police were working with the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency to track down the individuals and the syndicate involved.
He also said the Royal Malaysia Police were awaiting confirmation on whether the syndicate involved politicians in the Philippines, as reported by the media there.
On October 1, Laotian police seized 521 kilograms of crystal methamphetamine inside a Learjet private aircraft that had arrived from Subang at Luang Prabang International Airport in Laos.

Following the incident, 13 individuals, including Malaysian, Singaporean and Philippine nationals, were detained by Laotian authorities to assist investigations into the transnational drug trafficking case.
On October 7, police arrested a local man, the owner of the private jet, during a raid at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport. — Bernama
5a6462bac20798f5: JOHOR BARU: A teenage girl has put her education on hold to care for her parents, both battling stage four cancer.
The family is struggling to raise RM10,000 for each cycle of her mother's urgent chemotherapy.
Nur Sara Ayryna, who stopped attending school to look after her parents, now faces the heartbreaking reality of seeing both of them fight for their lives.
Her mother, Noor Diana Hashim, 47, was diagnosed with breast cancer, which has now spread to her liver, lungs, spine and neck.
Her father, — 47-year-old Iman Heart nasyid band frontman Zek Ayry Khan Zarak Khan — has nasopharyngeal cancer.
Both are unable to work and cannot afford treatment.
Noor Diana is now dependent on oxygen around the clock.
They are appealing for help because time is running out. Noor Diana needs to undergo chemotherapy as soon as possible.
She was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2021 and underwent surgery the following year.
The doctors recommended urgent chemotherapy. However, delays due to patient waiting lists had forced the family to consider private treatment, which costs about RM10,000 per cycle.
Noor Diana's left arm is swollen; it developed after her breast surgery, had worsened and further restricted her movement.
The couple's eldest son is employed, while their second son works as a motorcycle mechanic.
The couple had managed an event management company and actively volunteered to help the needy, including asnaf, single mothers, people with disabilities and flood victims, in the past.

"We were blessed with good health then and never missed opportunities to help others. Now, we are the ones being tested, and we appeal for help so my wife can receive the treatment she needs," Zek said.
0df2a7ba8122917e: KUALA LUMPUR: Enam cip semikonduktor baharu hasil inovasi tempatan mencerminkan kemajuan Malaysia daripada sebuah pusat pengeluaran kepada negara yang berupaya mereka bentuk, membangunkan dan memiliki teknologi sendiri, kata Menteri Ekonomi Akmal Nasrullah Nasir.

Dalam ucapan sempena AiSEM@SELANGOR 2026, Akmal berkata enam inovasi itu memperlihat keupayaan untuk melangkah daripada pembuatan kepada penciptaan dan pemilikan teknologi, selepas lima dekad membina nama sebagai negara yang dipercayai dalam industri semikonduktor dunia.

"Saya dimaklumkan bahawa keenam-enam inovasi ini mempunyai anggaran potensi jualan tergabung kira-kira RM300 juta, sekali gus menonjolkan peluang komersial bagi teknologi semikonduktor buatan tempatan," katanya.

"Semoga enam inovasi yang diperkenalkan pada hari ini menjadi pemangkin kepada lebih banyak teknologi tempatan yang berjaya dikomersialkan dan memperkukuh kedudukan Malaysia dalam rantaian nilai global."

Majlis hari ini menonjolkan MARS1000 buatan SkyeChip iaitu pemproses 'edge-AI' bagi kegunaan kamera, robot, dan sistem kilang; serta aiDAPTIV+ buatan MaiStorage iaitu solusi penstoran untuk komputer peribadi dan pelayan berasaskan kecerdasan buatan.

Turut diketengahkan peranti 'field-programmable gate array' buatan SiliconX untuk aplikasi industri serta automotif; serta Maxwell buatan Infinecs, iaitu pengawal atur 'low-dropout' gred automotif untuk menstabilkan bekalan kuasa bagi elektronik kenderaan.
Selain itu, cip pengawal kuasa buatan Weeroc Space bagi kegunaan satelit dan sistem penerokaan angkasa lepas, serta FC Mini buatan Alphaswift iaitu pengawal penerbangan untuk dron berautonomi.
"Hari ini, kami mempamerkan enam inovasi semikonduktor buatan tempatan yang dibangunkan oleh syarikat-syarikat di Malaysia Semiconductor IC Design Park," katanya.
"Pencapaian ini juga memberi inspirasi kepada generasi muda bahawa mereka mampu membina kerjaya berkualiti dan mencipta teknologi bertaraf dunia di Malaysia."

Industri semikonduktor menjadi penyumbang penting kepada ekonomi negara. FMT melaporkan pada Mac lalu bahawa sektor itu menyumbang kira-kira 6% kepada Keluaran Dalam Negara Kasar (KDNK), 26% kepada eksport dan 40% daripada pelaburan langsung asing yang diluluskan.

Menerusi Belanjawan 2027, Khazanah Nasional Bhd dan Kumpulan Wang Persaraan (Diperbadankan) (KWAP) akan melabur sebanyak RM1.2 bilion untuk menyokong syarikat semikonduktor tempatan bergerak ke segmen industri bernilai lebih tinggi.

Belanjawan itu juga menyediakan Dana Pelaburan Strategik bernilai RM100 juta yang akan diwujudkan oleh Khazanah Nasional Bhd dan InvestPenang bagi menyokong syarikat semikonduktor dan pembuatan termaju pada peringkat awal.
e3b5916d181e3241: HOUSTON: Tesla CEO Elon Musk unveiled what he described as a "flying" car, equipped with thrusters, during a livestreamed event at his SpaceX rocket company's facility on Thursday.
Technical and regulatory challenges have so far prevented the much-hyped flying car sector from getting off the ground.
Musk revealed his new Roadster sports car during a launch event at a SpaceX test facility in Texas.
During the demo, which was livestreamed on Tesla's X account, the car launched from a steep ramp and landed on its wheels.
"Flying cars are real," Musk said during the event.
He added that the vehicle's "success is not guaranteed" but that "it will probably work".
Musk said the car was equipped with "ultra high-pressure air tanks" to propel itself into the air.
The tech billionaire described the development as "what happens when you have a collaboration with the world's best car company and the world's best rocket company," referring to Tesla and SpaceX.
"The vehicle would go into production in 2028," he said.
American aviation pioneer Glenn Curtiss debuted the first flying car prototype in 1917.
However, successful designs have become more seriously contemplated only in recent years as electric motors and high-performance batteries have advanced.
bee05ba7f492dcf5: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian couple arrested with 5kg of cocaine at Tokyo's Haneda Airport on Oct 10 is believed to have invited three friends to act as drug mules while on holiday in Japan.
Bukit Aman criminal investigation department director Hussein Omar Khan said police believe that all five were aware that they were carrying drugs.
Hussein said they were each given a pair of shoes filled with drugs by a syndicate.

“The Sarawakian couple flew to KLIA before heading to Tokyo. They were paid RM8,000 each to act as drug mules and bring the shoes into Japan,” Utusan Malaysia quoted him as saying at the Johor police headquarters today.
He said the five engaged a Kuala Lumpur tour agent, who was unaware of the drugs, to arrange their flights to Tokyo.
“Checks found that none of them had criminal records. We are still investigating whether they have acted as drug mules in other countries before,” he said.
Hussein advised Malaysians to be cautious about offers to travel overseas.
"The public must also ensure their belongings are not used by syndicates to smuggle drugs," he said.

Fuji News Network previously reported that the five Malaysians were arrested at Haneda Airport after attempting to smuggle about 5kg of cocaine worth 120 million yen (RM3.1 million) concealed beneath their shoe insoles.
Each suspect allegedly carried about 1kg of cocaine, with 500g concealed beneath the insole of each shoe.
The five had taken possession of the drugs at Kuala Lumpur International Airport, the report said.
12ec3f7d2addad84: PUTRAJAYA: The proposed RM2,000 minimum wage was determined through economic research and extensive consultations with employers, workers and academics, rather than an arbitrary decision, National Wages Consultative Council chairman Tan Sri Zainal Rahim Seman said.
He said the council had conducted 21 engagement sessions nationwide and commissioned a comprehensive study to ensure the proposed rate was fair to workers without placing undue pressure on employers.
The study, supported by a government allocation of between RM1 million and RM1.5 million, examined several economic indicators to determine an appropriate minimum wage.
These included the poverty line income, median wages, price indices, labour growth and gross domestic product (GDP).
"We do not use figures arbitrarily. The rate is based on studies conducted by academics and consultants, and we believe it is appropriate and reasonable.
"It should not impose an undue burden on any party," he told reporters here.
Zainal said the council had also compared Malaysia's wage levels with those of other countries before arriving at its recommendations.
Based on median wages and other economic indicators, the study produced a projected wage range of about RM1,970 to more than RM2,100.
However, he said the council had to consider the interests of both workers and employers before recommending a rate.
"We held consultations with employers, workers and trade unions. We also have five academics, including university lecturers specialising in economics, who help us with the analysis," he said.
Zainal said the wage-setting process followed a tripartite approach involving the government, employers and workers.
The objective was to strike a balance between improving employees' purchasing power and ensuring businesses could manage their operating costs.
He acknowledged that implementing a new minimum wage could present challenges, recalling similar difficulties when Malaysia introduced its first minimum wage of RM900.
"There were problems when we first introduced the minimum wage. Implementation challenges will always exist, but our responsibility is to enforce it," he said.
Under the 2027 Budget, the government announced that the national minimum wage would increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month from June next year.
Micro, small and medium enterprises with annual sales below RM50 million will be exempted from the increase to allow them time to adjust.
9a5f9b99fd7ca58f: BANGKOK: Malaysia is strengthening its business environment, policy certainty and economic resilience to attract long-term investment, with foreign and domestic direct investments reaching record highs, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.

He said the government was reinforcing the country's economic fundamentals through regulatory clarity, business-friendly policies and reforms to provide investors with greater certainty when operating in Malaysia.
"Malaysia recorded gross domestic product growth of more than five per cent for two consecutive years while maintaining stable inflation, despite growing geopolitical uncertainties.
"Malaysia's story is resilience," he said at the Bloomberg Global Policy Series: ASEAN Growth Markets Spotlight – Competing and Connecting for Global Capital here on Friday.

Amir Hamzah said Malaysia was also focused on moving its economy up the value chain by strengthening key industries, including semiconductors, and deepening domestic supply chains to create higher-value jobs and enhance its competitiveness in global trade.

"We want to extend the supply chain and deepen the ecosystem," he said, adding that a stronger industrial ecosystem would develop local talent, improve supply chain reliability and strengthen Malaysia's position in global trade.

Amir Hamzah said the government was also seeking to expand the role of private markets in capital formation, enabling angel investors and venture capital to support businesses and strengthen the pipeline of companies entering public markets.

He said Malaysia's domestic capital base provided a strong foundation for growth, while improved corporate governance and value creation would help enhance the attractiveness of its capital market to international investors.

He also highlighted the importance of ASEAN integration, including better-connected capital markets, more efficient cross-border payment systems and the ASEAN Power Grid, in unlocking investment opportunities and strengthening regional supply chains.

Amir Hamzah said Malaysia would continue to focus on infrastructure development, economic diversification and consistent policy implementation to support sustainable growth and ensure its benefits reached the wider population.

"Whatever clarity that we've given, we've executed along that line. No surprises," he said, stressing that policy consistency and a supportive business environment remained central to Malaysia's investment appeal.
04ed296a1ae4f72c: ADDIS ABABA: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced Friday an interim administration would be established in the northern Tigray region, which has been controlled by rebels who have clashed with federal forces in recent weeks.

The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) launched a major offensive against government forces on Sept 23, before being pushed back and losing control of its strongholds, including the regional capital.
The region had been outside of Addis Ababa's control and did not participate in June federal elections, which were resoundingly won by Abiy's Prosperity Party.

The federal government caretaker administration, which aims to create "a stable political situation so that free and transparent elections can be held", will administer Tigray for the next six months, Abiy's office said on social media following a cabinet decision.
The TPLF leadership "did not desire peace", it said, instead initiating the latest "devastating war".

The region fought a 2020-22 war against federal forces -- supported by Eritrean troops -- which left an estimated 600,000 dead before a 2022 peace deal ended the fighting but provoked lingering discontent over the terms.

"In order for the people of Tigray to enjoy the peace that has eluded them, to ensure their right to self-governance, and to enjoy the benefits of development they have been deprived of for several years, they must break free from the cycle of conflict," the statement said.
In late September, the TPLF formed an uneasy alliance with several disparate armed groups opposed to the government.
The group has also moved closer to neighbouring Eritrea, long at odds with Ethiopia.
ec56cc246229d82e: KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) and Vietnam National Industry–Energy Group (Petrovietnam) have signed a strategic alliance agreement to strengthen cooperation across the energy value chain.

The agreement, which marks 35 years of collaboration between the two companies, will see them explore opportunities in upstream development, gas and liquefied natural gas, downstream activities and low-carbon solutions.

It was signed at Petrovietnam's headquarters by Petronas president and group chief executive officer Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik and Petrovietnam president and chief executive officer Le Manh Cuong.
The two companies subsequently exchanged documents at Vietnam's government headquarters in a ceremony witnessed by Prime Minister Le Minh Hung.
The exchange involved Tengku Muhammad Taufik and Petrovietnam chairman Le Ngoc Son.
In a statement, Petronas said it remained committed to supporting Vietnam's evolving energy needs while exploring broader opportunities for regional energy cooperation.
The national oil company entered Vietnam in 1991 as one of the country's pioneering foreign investors in the upstream oil and gas sector.
It has since expanded its presence into petrochemicals, renewable energy and LNG through partnerships with Petrovietnam and other Vietnamese companies.
Their cooperation also extends to regional initiatives, including a tripartite renewable energy project involving Malaysia, Vietnam and Singapore.
78ceb769c9d738b2: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed higher against the US dollar today, supported by Malaysia’s higher-than-expected advance GDP estimate for the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 2026).
Earlier today, the statistics department, in its Advance GDP Estimates for Q3 2026 report, said the economy expanded by 5.3% in Q3, after registering 6% growth in the preceding quarter.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Afzanizam Rashid told Bernama that the latest announcement suggests the Malaysian economy remains fairly resilient.
“It would not be a surprise if the whole-year GDP comes in higher than the current projection of 4.8% to 5.3%, with the nine months of 2026 (M9 2026) GDP growth already at 5.5%.
“We sense that the anticipation for a normalisation in overnight policy rate (from the pre-emptive cut in July 2025) would gather pace in light of the current growth trajectory,” he said.
At 6pm, the ringgit rose to 4.0795/4.0835 against the greenback from yesterday's close of 4.0800/4.0835.
At the close, the ringgit traded mostly lower against a basket of major currencies.

It increased against the Japanese yen to 2.5831/2.5895 from 2.5869/2.5892 at yesterday’s close but decreased against the euro to 4.5911/4.5956 from 4.5761/4.5801 and inched down against the British pound to 5.4396/5.4449 from 5.4101/5.4147.
Against its Asean peers, the local currency gained against the Indonesian rupiah to 226.3/226.6 from 227.4/227.7 and edged down against the Philippine peso at 6.48/6.49 from 6.47/6.48.
It was lower against the Singapore dollar at 3.1889/3.1922 from 3.1818/3.1848 at yesterday’s close and decreased against the Thai baht to 12.2101/12.2268 from 12.1758/12.1914.
c54ecedc797bb2a1: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are forecast across Perlis, Melaka, Putrajaya and parts of nine other states until 8 pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).

In Kedah, the affected areas include Kubang Pasu, Sik, Baling, Kuala Muda, Langkawi and Padang Terap, while in Perak, the weather alert covers Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Larut, Matang and Selama, Kerian, Kinta, Perak Tengah, Manjung, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk.
In Kelantan, the warning covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah and Machang, while in Terengganu, it affects Kemaman, Dungun and Hulu Terengganu.

In Pahang, the areas involved are Jerantut and Kuantan, while in Selangor, they comprise Petaling, Klang, Kuala Selangor, Kuala Langat, Sepang, Sabak Bernam and Hulu Langat, alongside Tampin in Negeri Sembilan.
In Sarawak, the alert covers Kuching, Samarahan, Serian, Sri Aman, Betong, Mukah, Sarikei, Sibu, Kapit (Song), Bintulu, Limbang and Miri (Marudi, Bario and Telang Usan).

In Sabah, the warning involves the Interior (Sipitang, Tenom, Pensiangan, Membakut, Beaufort, Tambunan, Keningau and Sook), West Coast (Kota Belud, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Papar, Penampang and Ranau), Sandakan (Kinabatangan and Tongod) and Kudat (Kota Marudu). — Bernama
404f8ec42e77f4e2: It might not be the Year of the Linux Desktop yet, but it could be the Year of Corporate Compliance on the Linux Desktop as Microsoft releases Defender for Linux Workstations. The product is an extension of Microsoft's existing Defender for Endpoint. According to the Windows behemoth, it brings "enterprise-grade protection, detection, vulnerability management and response capabilities to Linux workstations." Linux desktop users will get services including Defender's anti-virus functionality. The penguin-primed product also has management tools for inventory and security settings, as well as device isolation. "The result," said Microsoft, "is broader Linux protection, delivered through the tools and processes security teams already trust." The release is currently in public preview and requires the standalone Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 or Microsoft 365 E5 and E7. Support is based on the underlying Linux distribution and kernel version, with RHEL, CentOS, Ubuntu LTS, SUSE Linux Enterprise Server, and Oracle Linux among others on the list. There's no separate desktop agent to deploy or maintain. Defender works the same way as it does on Linux servers, so administrators shouldn't face many challenges. End users… well… that's another story. As enterprises gain visibility into Linux workstations alongside the rest of their endpoint estate, some friction is possible and it won't be technical. For some, compliance through Microsoft's tooling is anathema, no matter how penguin-friendly it claims to be nowadays. As for the why, we're told it's simple business and customer demand. Microsoft noted that more developers are using Linux desktops, which in turn makes them more attractive to attackers. "As Linux adoption expands beyond the datacenter, organizations need a consistent approach to protecting Linux wherever it is used," Microsoft said. The idea of Microsoft Defender being able to peer at Linux desktops may alarm some, but Microsoft announced Defender ATP for Linux back in 2020. The better question is: why has it taken so long? We'd also quibble with the premise "As more developers begin to use Linux desktops." Many already do: the 2025 Stack Overflow survey had Windows leading for professional work at 49.5 percent, but Ubuntu wasn't far behind at 27.7 percent. So less "begin," more "enthusiastically continue." ®
0745649d7e523d9e: WASHINGTON, Oct 16 — New White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia acknowledged today that she had failed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the United States, as her credentials face scrutiny.
Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and on social media, and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.

But the legal credentials of the press secretary, who President Donald Trump appointed last week, were called into question after she gave an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam.
The 41-year-old graduated from Pepperdine University’s law school in 2011, but obtaining a law degree does not automatically qualify someone to practice law.
In a Fox News interview on Thursday, host Sean Hannity asked Zacharia: “You took the bar exam, but you didn’t pass the bar exam, correct?”

In a separate interview with conservative media outlet Real America’s Voice on Thursday, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was “distracted and overwhelmed” by plans to move to China with her husband.
“The results are somewhat inconsequential because I knew I wouldn’t need the bar in China,” she said.
Foreign nationals cannot sit China’s bar exam, although they can undertake certain legal work at Chinese law firms.
Hannity later asked Zacharia if she had ever taken the bar exam a second time, to which she said: “I did not.”
“I had four kids in six years,” she said. “It was never my intent to go into the practice of law.”

Zacharia said on Real America’s Voice that “many people in the field” had assured her that she could “label myself a lawyer,” given her law degree and experience in business law gained in China, where she worked at a Beijing law firm.
She added that she could “provide legal analysis, not legal advice.”
“I was very careful how I executed this.”
The Campaign for Accountability, a political ethics organization, called on Wednesday for the California Bar Association to launch an investigation.
“In California, calling yourself a lawyer without a license isn’t puffery; it’s a crime,” the organization said in a press release.
Zacharia held her first White House press briefing on Tuesday with an unusually short press conference, answering questions from only three journalists.
She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, a loyal Trump supporter and often combative press secretary, who stepped down in August to care for her young children. — AFP
dbb80731d80a6390: PARIS, Oct 16 — After weeks of student protests, France is set to be swept by broader, nationwide demonstrations Saturday over the cost of living, setting up a potentially fraught period ahead of presidential elections next year.

The prospect of the two movements merging, perhaps with outbreaks of violence, poses a big challenge to the government — and an opportunity for far-left and far-right presidential candidates jockeying for power.

The country’s Yellow Vest movement, which eight years ago staged street protests against President Emmanuel Macron and his government, called Saturday’s “yellow and youth” demonstrations and urged millions to turn out.
It has appealed to teachers, workers, pensioners and farmers, as well as students, in an online call spread through social media.
“I have a feeling that (Saturday) will be a sort of culmination,” 18-year-old Marie-Lou, a protesting university student in the city of Lille, told AFP.
“We’ll be joined by workers and by the Yellow Vests, who are also mobilising again. There’s a sense of hope that all these different struggles might converge.”
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said Thursday he feared clashes after what he called “urban violence” during the student protests.
Lecornu is under pressure to get a cost-cutting budget through parliament. It aims to tackle France’s growing public debt by raising more tax revenue and reducing expenditures.
Yet the Yellow Vest and student movements are demanding the government spend more money.
They want protection from inflation sent surging above three percent by the Middle East war, and boosted public services, particularly education.
Anger at police
There is also public anger at perceived police brutality during the student protests, during which several teenage protesters were maimed and thousands were arrested.

Francois Boulo, a figure within the Yellow Vest movement, told AFP there was no coordination with the various groups expected to take part Saturday, “but we all had the same reaction when we saw the police violence against the students”.

The growing unrest on France’s streets and the country’s fragmented political system are weighing on the final months of Macron’s presidency, ahead of elections in April and May to choose his successor.
They are also fertile ground for opposition parties and their candidates.
Jean-Luc Melenchon, leader of the far-left France Unbowed party, has backed the student protests and marched in a demonstration Tuesday supporting them.
Far-right leader Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner according to surveys, has positioned her National Rally party on the side of the police, consistent with its law-and-order messaging.
Macron this week said he believed the “legitimate” demands of the protesting students were being “exploited for political purposes”, according to a government spokeswoman.
Prepared for violence
Organisers of tomorrow’s demonstrations have set up a website showing more than 500 demonstrations planned across France.
The Paris police banned a major march through the tourist and business heart of the capital, saying it could only take place in the east of the city.
But authorities and demonstrators were both preparing for possible violence.
Paris police have launched legal action against an influencer on Twitch who urged his hundreds of thousands of followers to take part in the demonstration “war zone”.

And on Friday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told France 2 television that officers could use stun grenades in case of “extremely serious urban violence”. He had previously suspended their use during the student protests after one stun grenade blew off the hand of a 15-year-old.
Demonstrators have set up a smartphone app giving the real-time location of police, tear gas and helicopters. — AFP
63795d8312396821: With his war in Iran and siding with Russia, it’s hard to think of someone who has done more to make the world a safer place It might have been more, shall we say, diplomatic if Donald Trump had taken some deep breaths after finding out he had been overlooked for the Nobel peace prize for the second year running before virtually declaring war on Norway. But maybe we should just be grateful he refrained from rubbishing the South African human rights activist Navi Pillay, who picked up the award, and shelved his plans to livestream the execution of the Norwegian prize committee. There again, you can understand his frustration. It’s hard to think of someone who has done more to make the world a safer place. Where would we be had not The Donald started a war with Iran which he shows no sign of knowing how to finish and which has forced up the price of global energy? And it was so good to see him intervening so positively in Russia’s war with Ukraine by appearing to side with the aggressor. These are just the things everyone is looking for in a Nobel peace laureate. The president is also put out that no one has noticed he has personally ended eight global conflicts; though it would be helpful if he could let us know which ones. Are they ones he has personally started – Trump appears disappointed that Argentina hasn’t invaded the Falklands again – or ones that only he knows about. During a press conference at Chequers in 2025, he claimed to have brought about a lasting peace between Albania and Azerbaijan. Maybe there are other wars going on we just don’t know about. Perhaps Australia and New Zealand have been bombing each other for years with neither side noticing. And perhaps the border between France and Italy has been a no-go zone ever since the fight between Zinedine Zidane and Marco Materazzi in the 2006 World Cup final. Still, Trump looks a cert to retain Gianni Infantino’s Fifa peace prize – if only because it seems likely to be scrapped, making him the only winner. Continue reading...
80e6c38df5d04f95: PETALING JAYA: A mechanic was sentenced to five years' jail by the sessions court here today after he pleaded guilty to attempting to murder a police corporal by ramming his car into him near Damansara Damai last week.
Judge Noor Ruzilawati Mohd Nor meted out the punishment to Tan Teek Lai, 33, and ordered that he serve the jail sentence from the date of his arrest on Oct 10.

According to the charge, Tan attempted to murder Muhamad Firdaus Maulud by ramming his car into him, causing him to suffer a fracture to his left arm, at Jalan Sungai Buloh-Kepong in Damansara here at 6.21pm on Oct 9.
The charge was framed under Section 307 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years, upon conviction.
The court was told that personnel from a mobile patrol unit spotted a suspiciously driven vehicle and ordered the driver to stop.
However, Tan refused to cooperate and fled, ramming into several vehicles.
Firdaus then attempted to pull Tan out of the vehicle, but the driver accelerated the car again, causing the policeman to suffer a fracture to his left arm.
Deputy public prosecutor Nurfadzlin Zulhasnan sought a stiff sentence, citing the public interest and the need to deter members of the public from committing similar offences.
However, Tan, who was unrepresented, appealed for a lighter sentence, saying that he was caring for his elderly and ailing parents.
He also pledged not to repeat the offence and apologised to the victim.
16c969edcf0adedd: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) will provide full cooperation to the Royal Malaysia Police to ensure that investigations into the accident that claimed the life of one of its personnel at KM256 of the North-South Expressway, near the Senawang exit last night, are conducted thoroughly and transparently.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said appropriate action would be taken against any party found to have violated the law or committed misconduct or negligence, based on the investigation findings.

“If there are any legal violations, misconduct or negligence identified through the investigation, appropriate action will be taken against the responsible parties in accordance with the provisions of the law and regulations in force,” he said in a statement today.
Loke expressed deep sorrow and extended his condolences to the family of Negeri Sembilan JPJ Enforcement Assistant Grade KP2 Mohd Azrul Rashid Yaakub, who was killed in the accident while on duty.

“The passing of Mohd Azrul is a great loss, particularly to his family and colleagues who have served alongside him. His sacrifice and dedication in carrying out his duties for the safety of road users will always be appreciated,” he said.

Loke also prayed for a speedy recovery for Motor Vehicle Examiner Grade AB2 Nor Amirudin Rameli, who suffered serious injuries in the incident, and for ease in all matters throughout his medical treatment.
He added that JPJ director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli visited the families of both officers this morning to convey his condolences and offer support.

Loke said the Transport Ministry and JPJ would continue to look into the welfare and needs of the deceased officer’s family and the injured officer, including ensuring that appropriate assistance was channelled to them.

Earlier, media reports said one JPJ personnel had died while another was seriously injured in an accident involving the department’s vehicle and two lorries on the southbound North-South Expressway near the Senawang exit last night.
The incident occurred at about 10.50pm while JPJ personnel were inspecting a lorry in the emergency lane.
Another lorry approaching from behind allegedly lost control before crashing into the JPJ sport utility vehicle (SUV) and the lorry being inspected. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: JPJ stands for Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan, or the Road Transport Department in English.
654f5b067370850c: BANGKOK: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark renewed calls on Friday for regulating artificial intelligence (AI), saying that allowing companies to continue to operate without robust legislation was like letting a race car loose on the streets at night without brakes.

"It's remarkable to me that the toys I buy for my children are regulated more than the literal super intelligence I work on at my day job," he told an event at the IMF-World Bank's Annual Meetings in Bangkok.
Clark said that US president Donald Trump, whose administration has called for the industry to police itself, was against the idea of regulation but that China was not.
"I think it's Formula One at night without maybe brakes in the cars," he said.
He said the lack of clarity around the will for regulation meant "the Formula One car is roaring round and nobody seems to want to put up a guardrail?"
At an industry summit in Dublin on Wednesday, calls to prioritise safety in the development of powerful AI technology dominated the conversation.
Concerns about AI guardrails have soared after models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic were involved in security incidents during testing, piling on pressure to regulate the technology.
A recent Anthropic report suggested small AI models may be only months away from behaving like computer worms, copying themselves from one internet-connected device to the next.
Anthropic has been among those companies calling for governments to step in, even suggesting international coordination to slow down the whole industry - including Chinese rivals.
That initiative has so far failed to materialise, with companies involved in a hyper-competitive race to attract as much investment as possible.
a312af083014581c: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The registration of persons with disabilities (OKU) follows the OKU Registration Guidelines (2019 Amendment), jointly developed by the Social Welfare Department (JKM) and the Health Ministry.
In a statement today, JKM said the process also involves medical specialists who sit on the OKU Registration Committee under the National Council for Persons with Disabilities.
The department said the guidelines ensure the evaluation and registration process is conducted professionally, systematically and based on established criteria.
Medical officers, practitioners or specialists assess an individual’s functionality and disability using the OKU Registration Application Form (BPPOKU Amendment 2/2019), it said.
JKM added that the assessment measures an individual’s level of functioning across seven domains, including self-care, mobility and dexterity.
The OKU Registrar will not approve applications that fail to meet the criteria in the relevant domains.
“However, applicants have the right to appeal the decision under Section 24 (2) of the Persons with Disabilities Act 2008,” JKM said.
The department stressed that individuals requiring welfare support will receive due consideration based on their needs and existing policies.
It remains committed to ensuring the well-being of vulnerable groups through appropriate aid and services tailored to individual needs. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: OKU stands for Orang Kurang Upaya, the Malay term for persons with disabilities. JKM stands for Jabatan Kebajikan Masyarakat, or the Social Welfare Department in English.
9294201b5e5aaabd: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan had identified its candidates for the Melaka state election two years ago, said the coalition’s election director, Amirudin Shari.
“We did it (identified the candidates) a long time ago,” he said when asked if PH had decided on its candidates for the Nov 14 election.
He said PH chairman Anwar Ibrahim and the component party leaders will finalise the list before announcing the candidates on Oct 24.
Asked if PH will field many new faces, Amirudin only said the candidates come from diverse backgrounds.
“There are young candidates and experienced ones. Some of them have careers," he told reporters after attending the launch of six homegrown semiconductor innovations here today.
Nominations for the Melaka election will take place on Oct 31, and early voting is set for Nov 10.
7ba84cd435083e34: PETALING JAYA: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim telah mengarahkan Menteri di Jabatan Perdana Menteri (Undang-Undang dan Reformasi Institusi) Azalina Othman Said untuk meneruskan rundingan lanjut berhubung rang undang-undang (RUU) bagi mengehadkan tempoh jawatan perdana menteri serta mengasingkan peranan peguam negara dengan pendakwa raya, susulan maklum balas daripada Majlis Raja-Raja.
Jurucakap kerajaan Fahmi Fadzil berkata, Azalina akan mengadakan sesi libat urus dengan Jawatankuasa Pilihan Khas Parlimen yang terlibat dalam penggubalan pindaan perlembagaan berkenaan.
Fahmi memaklumkan, Anwar telah memberi taklimat kepada Jemaah Menteri hari ini mengenai persembahan RUU tersebut kepada Raja-Raja Melayu serta maklum balas yang diterima.
“Selepas itu, sebarang pindaan atau penambahbaikan perlu dibawa semula ke Majlis Raja-Raja,” kata menteri komunikasi itu pada sidang media pasca-Kabinet hari ini

Semalam, Pejabat Penyimpan Mohor Besar Raja-Raja menyatakan bahawa Majlis Raja-Raja telah meneliti kertas rundingan bagi RUU Perlembagaan (Pindaan) 2026, yang mencadangkan had tempoh perkhidmatan perdana menteri.
Raja-Raja Melayu turut diberi taklimat mengenai Rang Undang-Undang Perlembagaan (Pindaan) (No. 2) 2026, yang bertujuan mengasingkan peranan peguam negara dan pendakwa raya.

RUU bagi mengehadkan tempoh perkhidmatan perdana menteri itu dibentangkan buat kali pertama pada 23 Feb lepas, namun gagal memperoleh sokongan majoriti dua pertiga yang diperlukan semasa bacaan kali kedua pada 2 Mac apabila kekurangan dua undi.

Sementara itu, RUU untuk mengasingkan peranan peguam negara dengan pendakwa raya kali pertama dibentangkan pada 23 Feb. Bacaan kali keduanya bagaimanapun ditangguhkan pada 14 Julai bagi membolehkan kerajaan membentangkan cadangan pindaan berkenaan kepada Majlis Raja-Raja.
f553092fe8d50d13: Landslide blocks river and triggers downstream flooding, while summer temperatures persist in Portugal Flash floods have swept through Nepal’s central Gorkha district after a pre-dawn landslide on 11 October blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, triggering severe downstream flooding. Two villages in the worst-affected Chumanubri rural municipality were reportedly destroyed, with homes, roads and bridges washed away. Part of a hydropower station was also damaged. After river levels surged from 2 metres to nearly 8.5 metres within hours, the national disaster risk reduction and management authority reported that 204 homes were damaged, and more than 650 people had been affected. More than 100 foreign trekkers were stranded in the popular hiking region. The floods come just two months after catastrophic flooding and landslides devastated parts of the country on the border with Tibet, leaving thousands dead or missing. Continue reading...
21ee12bffd18754d: MANCHESTER: Manchester United travel to historic rivals Leeds on Sunday with pressure mounting on manager Michael Carrick, while Manchester City aim to extend their perfect Premier League start despite uncertainty over their future.
Brighton could be one of the big winners should City suffer severe sanctions for breaking financial rules.
The Seagulls are riding high, just two points behind second-placed Arsenal, ahead of their grudge match against Crystal Palace.
AFP Sport previews the key Premier League clashes this weekend.
Man Utd's worst start in 40 years

United are off to their worst league start in 40 years and were plunged further into chaos by defender Lisandro Martinez's attack on the club's hierarchy over a lack of investment in the squad after Tuesday's 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid.
The Argentine took aim at technical director Jason Wilcox after the Red Devils' main transfer business during the summer window focused on bringing in three midfielders.
But Martinez himself has been one of those most culpable for a miserable start to the campaign for his part in goals conceded to Fulham and Tottenham in recent weeks.
United have won just one of their opening six league games and were also dumped out of the League Cup by Brighton.
Leeds last beat the Red Devils at Elland Road back in 2002, but did inflict the only home defeat of Carrick's interim spell in charge last season when the sides met in April.
Carrick is under increasing pressure as the latest manager struggling to reverse a sharp decline at Old Trafford since Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013.
But he said the hostile atmosphere his side will face in Leeds gives United the perfect chance to bounce back.
"What a great game (on) Sunday to prepare for. It's a fantastic game for us, for the club, for the history, for the supporters," said Carrick.
"Everything to do with the game is a great game so we'll be ready for that."
City case leaves league in limbo

Manchester City sit pretty at the top of the table with six wins from six league games, but that could all count for nothing if they do not successfully overturn a guilty verdict on more than 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules.

Enzo Maresca's men shut out that distraction to win 3-0 at Liverpool last weekend and rallied impressively in the second half despite losing 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in a thrilling Champions League tie on Tuesday.
But the uncertainty over their future has left the entire league in limbo.
City deny any wrongdoing and the long-running case still has at least a few months left to run before the appeal process concludes and potential sanctions are announced.
"My underlying thought is none of this is good for football and there are no winners," said former England manager Gareth Southgate.
City can stretch their lead at the top to six points when Ipswich visit the Etihad on Saturday, with Arsenal not in action until 24 hours later at Nottingham Forest.
'Ruthless' Brighton eye Champions League
Arsenal's only defeat this season came in a 3-0 trouncing by Brighton, who could reach new heights this season with a clutch of the established giants struggling.
Brighton have soared through the divisions and into Europe on the back of owner Tony Bloom's expertise in data analytics.
But they are yet to play Champions League football.
Despite routinely selling their prized assets to wealthier clubs, Brighton's smart recruitment of both players and coaches has ensured they have continued to thrive.
That has also made them popular among neutrals, but manager Fabian Hurzeler wants his side to show their nasty side against rivals Palace on Sunday.

"We want to be ruthless. We want to create this energetic atmosphere where it makes it so hard to come to this place," said Hurzeler. "We have to keep building this together with our fans and not be the nice football club anymore."

2bb27732ec25876d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The High Court was told today that the Malaysian Government had overpaid Semantan Estate Sdn Bhd (1952) between RM400,000 and RM500,000 in compensation for the acquisition of 263.272 acres of land known as the Duta Enclave in 1956.

Finance Ministry Valuation and Property Services Department (JPPH) assistant director Tan Tat Khuan said his assessment valued the land in Mukim Batu at RM875,000, compared with the RM1.39 million paid by the government.
“Deducting my valuation of RM875,000 from the RM1.39 million already paid shows that the government overpaid by between RM400,000 and RM500,000.
“If the court accepts my valuation, no additional compensation should be paid to the plaintiff (Semantan Estate),” he said.
Tan, the government’s sole witness, was testifying during the compensation assessment hearing before Judge Roslan Mat Nor.
Under further questioning by senior federal counsel Nurhafizza Azizan, Tan confirmed that his assessment showed the government had overpaid.
In earlier proceedings, Tan testified that the government paid Semantan Estate RM1.39 million in compensation in 1965, exceeding his recommended amount.
He said he had also assessed the land using a different acreage and arrived at a compensation value of RM985,000.

Asked by Judge Roslan whether additional compensation would be payable based on that valuation, Tan said none would be due. However, he clarified that his recommended compensation amounts excluded interest.

During questioning by Semantan Estate’s lawyer Ira Biswas, Tan rejected suggestions that information obtained from valuers A.A. Wragg and A.I.G. Harding, who assessed the land in 1956 and 1958 respectively, amounted to hearsay because they had not testified in court.
“In my view, both reports are consistent and reliable,” he said.

On Nov 13, 2025, the Federal Court dismissed Semantan Estate’s application for leave to appeal against a Court of Appeal ruling that the Federal Territory Registrar of Titles was not required to register the 263.272-acre Duta Enclave land in the company’s name.
The decision upheld the government’s position, and the case was returned to the High Court for an assessment of compensation.

On June 24, 2025, the Court of Appeal ruled that Semantan Estate was not entitled to ownership of the land but was entitled to appropriate compensation based on its value in 1956, when it was acquired by the government.

The prime Jalan Duta site houses several landmarks, including the Inland Revenue Board complex, government buildings, the National Hockey Stadium, the Institute of Islamic Understanding Malaysia and the Federal Territory Mosque.
Semantan Estate sued the government for trespass in 2003, alleging that the land had been unlawfully acquired.
In 2009, Judicial Commissioner Zura Yahya ruled that Semantan Estate retained beneficial interest in the 263.27-acre site, which the government had unlawfully acquired and occupied. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The initials JPPH in Malay stands for Jabatan Penilaian dan Perkhidmatan Harta, or the Valuation and Property Services Department in English.

765b0918fea4ad20: Blue Origin announced a major expansion of its already considerable Florida launch facilities on Friday morning with the intent of eventually flying 150 rockets a year from there.

The company said it would add two additional launch pads for the New Glenn rocket, in addition to two already under construction at Cape Canaveral. The company is also investing heavily in a new manufacturing facility that will produce up to 150 upper stages for a larger variant of the New Glenn rocket.

Additionally, the company plans to procure two additional landing ships to catch and return the first stage of the New Glenn rocket (it currently has one, named Jacklyn). 590ec38a60edecd2: Android was designed for phones, but that hasn't stopped Google from trying to adapt the OS and its apps to larger machines over the years. Googlebooks are just the latest attempt after tablets, Chromebooks, and foldables induced little change in how people interact with Android software. These new Android-powered laptops are designed to pick up where the web-focused ChromeOS left off, offering premium hardware and native support for Android apps.

Google sees Googlebooks as an alternative to Windows and macOS, but these platforms are entrenched with decades of software and UI conventions that keep users locked in. Googlebooks have to offer something very special to steal users away from either of the dominant operating systems.

For devoted Android phone users, there are some cool things in Googlebook OS, but the Android roots of these machines are impossible to miss. Sometimes it feels like using a Chromebook, and sometimes it feels like using a giant phone. It almost never feels like using a premium laptop, and that's the problem.

3478d8e882e9ab34: PETALING JAYA: Sime Darby Bhd will be the key beneficiary of Chinese carmaker BYD’s tie up with a local car assembly partner for its completely knocked-down (CKD) vehicle operations in Malaysia, a research house said.

This follows BYD’s appointment of Sime Darby’s 54%-owned subsidiary Inokom Corp Sdn Bhd to assemble BYD electric vehicles (EVs) at its plant in Kulim, Kedah. The memorandum of understanding was signed yesterday at BYD’s headquarters in Shenzhen, China.
“While still pending further clarity on production volumes secured by BYD with Inokom, we view the pivot to contract assembly as positive for Sime Darby,” CGS International said in a note today.

The research house noted the higher production volumes could also improve economies of scale at Inokom, which can produce up to 80,000 units per year, with a utilisation rate of 80%. Sime Darby is also the official distributor of BYD vehicles in Malaysia since 2022.
Inokom is partly owned by South Korea’s Hyundai Motor Company and Bermaz Auto Bhd, which assembles Mazda vehicles.
BYD’s shift to contract assembly comes after scrapping its previous plan, announced in August 2025, for an assembly plant in Tanjung Malim, Perak, to produce up to 50,000 units a year.

However, the proposed facility was subsequently subjected to a requirement by the ministry of investment, trade and industry (Miti) for up to 80% of cars produced there to be exported. The remaining 20% would also need to be priced above RM200,000 per unit.

After news broke in March that BYD was having second thoughts about the Tanjung Malim plant, Miti came out to defend its conditions, calling them “non-discriminatory” and saying they apply to all high-volume automotive projects.
Opting for contract assemby via Inokom means BYD is effectively freed from the limits imposed as well as it benefits from tax exemption for locally-assembled EVs until 2027.
That should support the sustainability and competitiveness of Sime Darby's BYD distribution business in Malaysia, CGS noted.
It also said there is potential for an extension of the EV tax exemption given the government's focus on promoting local assembly.
BYD currently offers seven models in Malaysia though details of which models will be assembled locally have yet to be announced.
It has sold more than 35,000 vehicles since entering the Malaysian market, including over 7,500 units in the first half of this year.
f0a5f325be5a6595: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group has delayed the release of PostgreSQL 19, the latest iteration of the popular open source database, and held back an unusual number of features. Once slated for release in late September or early October, PostgreSQL 19 is now expected to be generally available around November 19. Developers have also dropped between eight and 10 significant features. Explaining the number of reverts — features whose rollouts have now been postponed to next year's release, PostgreSQL 20 — Peter Eisentraut, veep at EDB, a PostgreSQL support and consultancy, said the reason could be at least in part attributed to the LLM code reviews used by developers. In a blog post, Eisentraut, who is a leading PostgreSQL committer, said some of the reverted features had significant architectural defects that would have been hard to fix "quickly and during beta." However, the introduction of LLM-assisted code review also uncovered a long tail of “relatively harmless issues involving various edge cases” which, in past times, developers might not have noticed until much later, most likely issuing bug fixes in the five years following launch. “With LLM-assisted code review, these kinds of things can get found much faster, and then you’re staring at a list of forty defect reports. Even if each of them requires only a three-line fix on average, there is a fixed overhead to dealing with each of these, and then you run out of time.” When the big updates for PostgreSQL 19 were written, LLM-assisted code review was not as useful as it is now, we're told, but in the months leading up to the launch, the AI-supported reviews became better understood and more effective. “The effective quality bar has been raised after the time the feature was written and committed. Unless the capabilities of LLM-assisted code review keep improving at the current rate, this situation should sort itself out for future development cycles,” Eisentraut said. He was also at pains to point out that the reverts were not down to “vibe coding” in development, as the technique was not available when most of the new features were written. Postgres was first proposed by Michael Stonebraker in 1986. In 1994, Andrew Yu and Jolly Chen replaced the query language POSTQUEL with SQL, and in 1995 made the database freely available and modifiable under a more permissive license, renaming it PostgreSQL. It has since become the most popular database among professional developers owing to the services the big three hyperscalers built on it as well as the range of wire-compatible distributed systems available. Among the features pulled from the PostgreSQL 19 iteration is support for SQL Property Graph Queries (SQL/PGQ), which became part of the SQL standard in 2023. The feature provides syntax for exploring relationships between nodes connected by edges. PostgreSQL's implementation was removed over unresolved issues. At the time, PostgreSQL contributor Tom Lane warned: "At this point I'd be willing to bet dinner that if we ship it in v19 there will be post-release bug discoveries that are unfixable until v20." Despite the delay, Eisentraut promises PostgreSQL 19 will still be “a great release,” that includes REPACK CONCURRENTLY, which avoids the table-lock VACUUM FULL operation used to reclaim disk space. “And it will be very robust, after all the additional scrutiny,” he said. The features reverted from PostgreSQL 19 will likely make it into PostgreSQL 20. Just a few months ago, developers expected PostgreSQL 20 to have no new features, just bug fixes. Now, it is likely to have the new features left over from the earlier release, Eisentraut said.®

b29a4442329aad38: MADRID: Mainland Spain sizzled in its warmest September since records began in 1961, with exceptional heat effectively making it another summer month, national weather agency AEMET said on Friday.

The announcement is the latest in a series of new temperature records this year across Europe, scorched by successive summer heatwaves that scientists say were turbo-charged by human-driven climate change.
The average temperature in September was 22.5C, 3.4C above the norm for the 1991-2020 reference period, said AEMET, with the unprecedented reading coming after Spain's hottest summer on record.
It was the first time the figure for September exceeded the average summer temperature of 22.1C for the 1991-2020 period, AEMET added in a statement.
The country equalled its all-time heat record for the month when 45.7C was registered in the southwestern municipality of El Granado on Sep 3.

AEMET briefly issued the highest red alert for heat in small areas of the southern region of Andalusia in September, the first time such warnings had been sent in the month since they started in 2007.
Last month was also extremely dry, recording just 36% of the normal rainfall expected in September in mainland Spain based on the 1991-2020 reference period.
Extreme temperatures have been linked to tens of thousands of excess deaths across the continent, as well as disrupting daily life and the economy through drought and low river levels.

69149006e8d19170: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — When Malaysian model Vibha Rajish auditioned for what she thought was an ordinary sportswear commercial, she had no idea she would soon be sharing the screen with Hollywood star Zendaya.
In fact, the 23-year-old almost skipped the audition altogether because she had a wedding to attend in Belgium.
Instead, her decision to give it a shot landed her a role in an action-packed campaign for Swiss sportswear brand On, featuring Zendaya in a cinematic showdown with a group of female martial artists.

Titled Zendaya in Your New Favourite Action Movie, the two-minute campaign film opens against a striking backdrop of brutalist concrete architecture, with Zendaya being pursued through the city by a group of fighters.
Vibha makes a fleeting appearance between the 1:08 and 1:11 marks, playing one of the martial artists targeting the actress.
Released on YouTube on October 1, the campaign marked a significant milestone for Vibha, who told Malay Mail she felt emotional, grateful and proud to have been part of the production.
“It was so surreal that this little girl from Bandar Utama was about to meet, let alone act alongside Zendaya in her prime,” she said.
When ‘Z’ turned out to be Zendaya
Vibha’s brush with Hollywood began with an unusually vague casting call for a “sportswear ad”.
The only instruction was to turn up wearing sportswear.
With a wedding in Belgium already on her calendar, she initially considered giving the audition a miss.
She eventually went along, and just two days before filming, learnt that she had landed the job and needed to return for the shoot.
At the time, she saw it as an opportunity to earn some extra money for her summer holidays.
What she didn’t know was that she was about to work alongside Zendaya — or that the actress’s celebrated stylist, Law Roach, would also be involved in the production.
“Initially there was no mention of Z (as we called her on set).
“I arrived on set for the rehearsals and passed two unusually large trailers.
“Didn’t think much of it.
“Until I met the other girls who had been training since the week before, and they asked how I was feeling.
“‘Feel about what?’ I remember saying, and everyone started laughing.
“Then they broke the news to me: the Z on the trailer I passed was for Zendaya, and the L trailer was for Law Roach (who I’m also obsessed with),” she added.
For a young Malaysian model who had arrived expecting a straightforward commercial shoot, it was quite the revelation.
And despite the hectic filming schedule, Vibha found Zendaya to be warm and considerate towards everyone on set.
The actress even offered her pizza — although nerves got the better of her.
“It was a very hectic few days but yes! She was lovely to everyone, she even offered me pizza.
“No, I didn’t take it cos I was too nervous and freaked out lol,” she shared.
From Bandar Utama to Prague
Born in Kuala Lumpur and raised in Petaling Jaya, Vibha describes her childhood as quintessentially Malaysian, with her schools all located within a 2km radius of her family home.
“I feel like I had a pretty standard Malaysian upbringing.
“I went to the tadika (kindergarten) in my taman, SJKC then SMK, all within a 2km radius of my house,” she said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Malaysian model Vibha Rajish (right) appears in On’s action-packed campaign video, ‘Zendaya in Your New Favourite Action Movie’. — Picture via YouTube/On and Law Roach
Her journey into modelling began at 16, when she was looking for a way to help pay for treatment for her beloved cat, MJ, who had been diagnosed with feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV).
With the Covid-19 pandemic making retail jobs difficult to come by, she enlisted the help of a neighbourhood friend who was an aspiring photographer.
The arrangement was simple: he would gain photography experience, while she would have photographs to help her pursue modelling opportunities.
“That’s where it all began!” she said.
Her next chapter took her to Prague, a city that had captured her imagination after she first encountered it in a fantasy book.
The Czech capital’s relatively affordable cost of living compared with other European cities also appealed to her as a place to study.
During her first year there, she was approached by a modelling scout and subsequently signed with an agency.
For a time, she balanced her studies with modelling assignments and part-time jobs to cover her living expenses.
“But since the last two years, modelling and acting have become my bread and butter.
“I love it here so much, but I also love spending the winter back home in Malaysia!” she said.
A homecoming in the making
Although the On campaign has given Vibha another memorable addition to her portfolio, her ambitions extend beyond modelling.
Having spent five years abroad, she is keen to explore more acting opportunities closer to home, particularly in Bahasa Malaysia.
“I would love to do some acting in Malaysia and in Bahasa specifically.
“My Malay has deteriorated a little since living abroad for five years, but I love a challenge and it would be so special to me to do something local.
“I’ll be back in January so I’m just excited to be back home, eat good food and see what Malaysia has in store for me,” she concluded.
9292d9e40b01e0bf: An old-fashioned smash-and-grab job on a photographer’s vehicle threatens the security of pupils’ data as a UK secondary school says it faces a potential data protection pickle. Jon Curtis-Brignell, headteacher at Priory School in Lewes, said in an email this week that a company the school hired to take pupils’ annual school photos has alerted it to a data theft case after a vehicle was broken into. “Pret-a-Portrait has informed us that, overnight between 6 and 7 October, one of its vehicles was broken into and a camera bag containing SD memory cards was stolen,” Curtis-Brignell wrote. “Some of these cards may have contained photographs taken at Priory School, together with images of the QR code cards used for school photographs, which show pupils’ names and class names.” The headteacher said that the same equipment used to take the photos at Priory School was also used for three additional photography jobs after Pret-a-Portrait visited the school on October 1. Pret-a-Portrait, which has offices in the UK, Qatar, and the UAE, told the school that it believes “most, if not all” of the files containing pupils’ data will have been overwritten as a result, but it cannot be certain. Curtis-Brignell said that the potentially affected information included photographs, pupils’ names, and their “class information associated with the photography process.” Other types of data, such as addresses, contact details, financial information, medical information, and safeguarding records stored in the school’s own systems remain untouched. Nick Kerr, owner of Pret-a-Portrait, told The Register that no physical, printed photos were stored in the vehicle at the time of the break-in, and that it was not possible to determine the potential scope of the data protection violation. “As the email from Priory School explains, it is likely to be somewhere between a small subset of their pictures and none of them,” said Kerr. On a positive note, he said that there is nothing to suggest the files have been improperly accessed. “Our analysis reveals that no improper access to pictures from this job occurred in between the time of the theft and the pictures being taken offline.” Per the headteacher’s email, Pret-a-Portrait confirmed that it took a number of steps to mitigate the potential damage, including taking all school photos offline, changing the IDs used to access them, and changing its procedures so that all SD cards are wiped at the end of each commission. The company also “reviewed and strengthened its procedures following the incident,” and reported the matter to both the police and the ICO. “I appreciate that receiving an email of this nature may understandably cause concern,” Curtis-Brignell added. “We have worked closely with our Data Protection Officer and Pret-a-Portrait to understand what happened, establish the potential risk and ensure that appropriate action has been taken. “We wanted to be open with families about what has happened, while also reassuring you that there is currently no evidence that the information has been accessed or misused and that a number of steps have now been taken to prevent access to the affected photographs and reduce the risk of a similar incident occurring again.” ®
